    "customer_id": "c81d4e5f-2a3b-4c5d-9e6f-7a8b9c0d1e2f",
    "warehouse_id": "w-7f2e9d1c-4b5a-4e6d-8c7f-3a2b1c0d9e8f",
    "status": "PACKED", "total_cents": 24850, "currency": "USD",
    "line_items": [
        {"line_id": "l-01", "sku_id": "a1b2c3d4-e5f6-7890-abcd-ef1234567890",
         "qty": 2, "unit_price_cents": 8999, "tax_code": "TX-NJ-066",
         "fulfillment": {"node": "w-east-2", "bin": "A-14-03", "pick_wave": 7}},
        {"line_id": "l-02", "sku_id": "0987fedc-ba65-4321-0fed-cba987654321",
         "qty": 1, "unit_price_cents": 6852, "tax_code": "TX-NJ-066",
         "fulfillment": {"node": "w-east-2", "bin": "B-02-11", "pick_wave": 7}},
    ],
    "audit": {"created_by": "svc-order-writer", "created_at": "2026-10-14T09:12:44Z",
              "updated_by": "svc-order-writer", "updated_at": "2026-10-14T11:03:02Z",
              "row_version": 14, "deleted_at": None, "change_seq": 881923},
    "internal_flags": {"fraud_score": 0.02, "manual_review": False, "batch_id": "b-551"},
}

# --- The agent-facing shape: flat, pruned, human-readable ----------------------
class OrderLine(BaseModel):
    sku: str
    qty: int
    unit_price: float = Field(description="Dollars, not cents")

class OrderSummary(BaseModel):
    """Everything an agent needs to reason about an order. Nothing it doesn't."""
    order_id: str = Field(description="Short human reference, e.g. o-9001")
    status: str
    total: float
    items: list[OrderLine]

server = MCPServer("pruning-mcp", version="1.0.0")

@server.tool()
def get_order_summary(order_id: str) -> str:
    """Return a compact, pruned order summary.

    Drops audit columns (created_by, row_version...), internal UUID join keys
    and fulfillment internals. Flattens cents to dollars and nested line items
    into one markdown block the model can actually reason over.
    """
    raw = RAW_ORDER  # in production: fetched from the Order service
    summary = OrderSummary(
        order_id="o-9001",
        status=raw["status"].lower(),
        total=raw["total_cents"] / 100,
        items=[OrderLine(sku=li["sku_id"][:8] + "…", qty=li["qty"],
                         unit_price=li["unit_price_cents"] / 100)
               for li in raw["line_items"]],
    )
    md = [f"# Order {summary.order_id} — {summary.status}",
          f"Total: ${summary.total:.2f}", "", "Items:"]
    md += [f"- {li.sku} × {li.qty} @ ${li.unit_price:.2f}" for li in summary.items]
    return "\n".join(md)

async def main() -> None:
    raw_text = json.dumps(RAW_ORDER, indent=2)
    result = await server.call_tool("get_order_summary", {"order_id": "o-9001"})
    pruned = result.content[0].text
    before, after = estimate_tokens(raw_text), estimate_tokens(pruned)
    print(pruned)
    print(f"\nraw payload:    {len(raw_text):5d} chars ≈ {before:5d} tokens")
    print(f"pruned summary: {len(pruned):5d} chars ≈ {after:5d} tokens")
    print(f"reduction:      {100 * (1 - after / before):.0f}% of context reclaimed")
    # The agent can no longer see (or hallucinate with) internal keys:
    for leaked in ("created_by", "row_version", "fraud_score", "c81d4e5f"):
        assert leaked not in pruned, f"internal field leaked: {leaked}"
    print("OK: audit columns, UUID keys and nesting stripped; nothing internal leaked.")

if __name__ == "__main__":
    asyncio.run(main())

Output:

# Order o-9001 — packed
Total: $248.50

Items:
- a1b2c3d4… × 2 @ $89.99
- 0987fedc… × 1 @ $68.52

raw payload:     1178 chars ≈   294 tokens
pruned summary:    96 chars ≈    24 tokens
reduction:      92% of context reclaimed
OK: audit columns, UUID keys and nesting stripped; nothing internal leaked.

Notice what the pruning deliberately destroyed:

  • the full UUIDs, replaced by an 8-character prefix the agent can quote back to a human but cannot join on;
  • the total_cents minor-unit convention, replaced by dollars, the way the business talks;
  • the entire audit and internal_flags blocks.

If some future agent genuinely needs the audit trail, that is a separate privileged tool with its own access control — not a field riding along on every read.

3.5 Pattern 3 — Read-vs-Write Separation

Why. MCP gives you two primitives and they have different physics. A resource is data the client reads: it can be cached, re-read cheaply, and subscribed to (resources/subscribe + notifications/resources/updated keeps the model's context fresh without polling). A tool is an action: it has side effects, a blast radius, and must never be cached or replayed silently. The 1:1 generator maps everything to tools, which throws away all three resource advantages and hands the model a catalog where reading the refund policy and issuing a refund look equally consequential. They are not.

The conversion rule is mechanical: GET endpoints that return reference or entity data become resources; POST/PUT/DELETE endpoints become tools. Reads get caching and subscriptions for free. Writes get something more valuable: a single choke point where you enforce guards — amount limits, state-machine transitions, approval gates — before the side effect happens. An agent cannot "accidentally" call a resource with a write semantic, because resources have no write semantic. That structural fact is worth more than any amount of prompt engineering telling the model to "be careful."

Runnable example. Refund policy and invoice schema are resources (stable, cacheable). Payments and refunds are tools (money moves, guards enforced). Note the over-refund guard inside issue_refund — the write choke point doing its job.

"""Pattern 3: Read-vs-Write Separation. Reads become MCP Resources (cacheable,
subscribable, safe); writes stay MCP Tools (audited, guarded, never cached)."""
import asyncio
import json
from mcp.server.mcpserver import MCPServer

server = MCPServer("billing-rw-mcp", version="1.0.0")

REFUND_POLICY = """# Refund policy (v2026-10)
- Full refund within 30 days of delivery, no questions asked.
- Partial refund after 30 days needs a support ticket reference.
- Refunds settle to the original payment method within 5 business days."""

INVOICE_SCHEMA = """# Invoice record (agent view)
invoice_id, order_id, amount, currency, status (issued|paid|void), issued_at"""

PAYMENTS: dict[str, dict] = {}
REFUNDS: dict[str, dict] = {}

# --- Reads: resources. The client may cache these and subscribe to updates. ---
@server.resource("enterprise://billing/refund-policy")
def refund_policy() -> str:
    """Stable reference text: safe to cache, cheap to re-read."""
    return REFUND_POLICY

@server.resource("enterprise://billing/invoice-schema")
def invoice_schema() -> str:
    """Field contract for invoice records, without internal columns."""
    return INVOICE_SCHEMA

# --- Writes: tools. Every call is an audited side effect, never cached. -------
@server.tool()
def post_payment(order_id: str, amount: float) -> dict:
    """Record a payment against an order. Side effect: money moves."""
    pid = f"pay-{len(PAYMENTS) + 1:04d}"
    PAYMENTS[pid] = {"payment_id": pid, "order_id": order_id, "amount": amount,
                     "status": "captured"}
    return {"payment_id": pid, "status": "captured", "amount": amount}

@server.tool()
def issue_refund(payment_id: str, amount: float, reason: str) -> dict:
    """Refund a captured payment. Side effect: money moves back.

    Blast-radius guard: refuses amounts larger than the captured payment.
    """
    payment = PAYMENTS.get(payment_id)
    if payment is None:
        return {"error": f"unknown payment {payment_id}"}
    if amount > payment["amount"]:
        return {"error": f"refund ${amount:.2f} exceeds captured "
                         f"${payment['amount']:.2f}"}
    rid = f"rfnd-{len(REFUNDS) + 1:04d}"
    REFUNDS[rid] = {"refund_id": rid, "payment_id": payment_id,
                    "amount": amount, "reason": reason}
    return {"refund_id": rid, "status": "issued", "amount": amount}

async def main() -> None:
    def result_of(call):  # in-process call_tool returns dict payloads as JSON text
        return json.loads(call.content[0].text)

    tools = [t.name for t in await server.list_tools()]
    resources = [str(r.uri) for r in await server.list_resources()]
    print("tools (writes):", tools)
    print("resources (reads):", resources)
    assert set(tools) == {"post_payment", "issue_refund"}
    assert "enterprise://billing/refund-policy" in resources

    policy = await server.read_resource("enterprise://billing/refund-policy")
    assert "30 days" in policy[0].content

    pay = await server.call_tool("post_payment",
                                 {"order_id": "o-9001", "amount": 248.50})
    pid = result_of(pay)["payment_id"]
    ok = await server.call_tool("issue_refund", {"payment_id": pid,
                                                 "amount": 100.0,
                                                 "reason": "partial return"})
    assert result_of(ok)["status"] == "issued"
    over = await server.call_tool("issue_refund", {"payment_id": pid,
                                                   "amount": 9999.0,
                                                   "reason": "oops"})
    assert "error" in result_of(over), "blast-radius guard failed"
    print(f"payment {pid} captured; partial refund issued; over-refund refused.")
    print("OK: reads are resources, writes are guarded tools.")

if __name__ == "__main__":
    asyncio.run(main())

Output:

tools (writes): ['post_payment', 'issue_refund']
resources (reads): ['enterprise://billing/refund-policy', 'enterprise://billing/invoice-schema']
payment pay-0001 captured; partial refund issued; over-refund refused.
OK: reads are resources, writes are guarded tools.

One subtlety worth naming: the catalog itself gets smaller. Every GET you convert to a resource is one fewer tool schema competing for the model's attention in tools/list. Pattern 3 therefore compounds with the anti-pattern fix from §3.1 — fewer tools, better selection, cheaper turns.

3.6 Pattern 4 — Pagination & Large Payload Protection

Why. Some legacy endpoint returns 10,000 rows. The generator turns it into a tool. One day the agent calls it, and 1.5 MB of JSON — roughly 393,000 tokens, measured below — lands in the context window. The session is over. Not degraded: over. The model starts dropping its own earlier reasoning to make room, tool results get truncated mid-object, and every subsequent call inherits the confusion. This is the only pattern in this module that protects against instant death rather than slow decay, so treat its guards as non-negotiable.

Three guards, applied together:

  1. Hard page cap, server-side. The tool accepts page_size but clamps it. The agent cannot ask for all 10,000 rows no matter how it phrases the request. A cursor (opaque, base64) replaces offset math the model would fumble.
  2. Server-side summarization. When the agent asks "how big is the ledger?", the question is about an aggregate, not rows. Compute the aggregate where the data lives and return 22 tokens, not 393,000.
  3. Resource URI pointers instead of raw dumps. For genuine bulk-export needs, return a pointer — a resource URI the agent can page through — and keep the decision (and the token budget) on the server side.

Runnable example. A 10,000-row ledger, the greedy request that tries to defeat the cap, cursor walk, aggregation, and the pointer.

"""Pattern 4: Pagination & Large Payload Protection. A 10,000-row ledger would
be ~393k tokens as one response — instant context death. Three guards: a hard
page cap, server-side summarization, and resource-URI pointers."""
import asyncio
import base64
import json
from mcp.server.mcpserver import MCPServer

def estimate_tokens(text: str) -> int:
    return max(1, len(text) // 4)

# --- 10,000 ledger rows, as the legacy GET /ledger would return them ----------
LEDGER = [
    {"seq": i, "entry_id": f"e-{i:05d}",
     "account": "4000-revenue" if i % 2 else "1100-cash",
     "amount": round(10 + (i * 37 % 900) + 0.99, 2), "memo": f"batch posting {i}",
     "audit": {"by": "svc-ledger", "seq": 900000 + i}}
    for i in range(10_000)
]

PAGE_MAX = 50  # hard ceiling: no single tool response may exceed this many rows

def encode_cursor(index: int) -> str:
    return base64.urlsafe_b64encode(str(index).encode()).decode()

def decode_cursor(cursor: str | None) -> int:
    if not cursor:
        return 0
    return int(base64.urlsafe_b64decode(cursor.encode()).decode())

server = MCPServer("ledger-mcp", version="1.0.0")

@server.tool()
def list_ledger_entries(cursor: str | None = None, page_size: int = 25) -> dict:
    """Page through the ledger. page_size is clamped to PAGE_MAX (50) — the
    agent cannot ask for all 10,000 rows in one call, no matter how it phrases it.
    """
    page_size = max(1, min(page_size, PAGE_MAX))
    start = decode_cursor(cursor)
    rows = LEDGER[start:start + page_size]
    next_cursor = (encode_cursor(start + page_size)
                   if start + page_size < len(LEDGER) else None)
    return {
        "entries": [{"entry_id": r["entry_id"], "account": r["account"],
                     "amount": r["amount"]} for r in rows],  # pruned: no audit block
        "page_size": page_size,
        "next_cursor": next_cursor,
        "total_rows": len(LEDGER),
    }

@server.tool()
def summarize_ledger() -> dict:
    """Server-side aggregation. When the agent asks 'how big is the ledger?',
    it gets the answer — not the ledger."""
    total = sum(r["amount"] for r in LEDGER)
    return {"total_rows": len(LEDGER),
            "total_amount": round(total, 2),
            "accounts": sorted({r["account"] for r in LEDGER})}

@server.tool()
def export_ledger() -> dict:
    """Pointer, not payload. The full export lives behind a resource URI the
    agent can page through; the tool response itself stays tiny."""
    return {"resource_uri": "enterprise://billing/ledger/full",
            "note": "Read via the resource in pages; do not request raw rows in chat."}

@server.resource("enterprise://billing/ledger/full")
def ledger_full() -> str:
    return json.dumps({"total_rows": len(LEDGER),
                       "hint": "use list_ledger_entries for pages"})

async def main() -> None:
    def result_of(call):
        return json.loads(call.content[0].text)

    full_text = json.dumps(LEDGER)
    print(f"naive full dump: {len(full_text) // 1024} KB ≈ "
          f"{estimate_tokens(full_text):,} tokens (would consume a whole context window)")

    # The agent tries to be clever and asks for everything at once:
    greedy = result_of(await server.call_tool(
        "list_ledger_entries", {"cursor": None, "page_size": 10_000}))
    assert len(greedy["entries"]) == PAGE_MAX, "page cap was bypassed!"
    assert greedy["next_cursor"] is not None
    print(f"greedy page_size=10000 → clamped to {len(greedy['entries'])} rows, "
          f"next_cursor issued")

    page2 = result_of(await server.call_tool(
        "list_ledger_entries", {"cursor": greedy["next_cursor"], "page_size": 25}))
    assert page2["entries"][0]["entry_id"] == "e-00050"
    print(f"cursor pagination walks forward: page 2 starts at "
          f"{page2['entries'][0]['entry_id']}")

    summary = result_of(await server.call_tool("summarize_ledger", {}))
    assert summary["total_rows"] == 10_000
    print(f"summarize_ledger: {summary['total_rows']:,} rows → "
          f"${summary['total_amount']:,.2f} in "
          f"~{estimate_tokens(json.dumps(summary))} tokens")

    export = result_of(await server.call_tool("export_ledger", {}))
    assert export["resource_uri"] == "enterprise://billing/ledger/full"
    print("export_ledger returns a resource pointer, not 10,000 rows.")
    print("OK: page cap enforced, aggregation server-side, pointers over payloads.")

if __name__ == "__main__":
    asyncio.run(main())

Output:

naive full dump: 1534 KB ≈ 392,944 tokens (would consume a whole context window)
greedy page_size=10000 → clamped to 50 rows, next_cursor issued
cursor pagination walks forward: page 2 starts at e-00050
summarize_ledger: 10,000 rows → $4,603,600.00 in ~22 tokens
export_ledger returns a resource pointer, not 10,000 rows.
OK: page cap enforced, aggregation server-side, pointers over payloads.

The numbers are the argument. 392,944 tokens versus 22. There is no prompt technique that survives the first number. Architecture has to prevent it.

3.7 Refactoring blueprint — "Enterprise Order & Billing"

Time to put the four patterns to work on one concrete domain. Below is a legacy OpenAPI surface for order and billing work — the kind of thing that accumulates over five years and three teams. Twelve endpoints:

# Endpoint Domain
1 GET /orders orders
2 GET /orders/{id} orders
3 POST /orders orders
4 PUT /orders/{id} orders
5 DELETE /orders/{id} orders
6 GET /invoices invoices
7 GET /invoices/{id} invoices
8 POST /invoices invoices
9 POST /payments payments
10 GET /payments/{id} payments
11 POST /refunds refunds
12 GET /refunds/{id} refunds

The redesign target: 3 tools + 2 resources. Here is the decision for each endpoint, in the order a reviewer would ask about them.

Merge into place_order (Pattern 1). POST /orders (#3), POST /invoices (#8), and POST /payments (#9) are not three things the agent wants. They are one thing: "take this customer's money for these items." The tool validates the customer, checks stock before any write, then creates the order, the invoice, and the payment as one business step, and returns a compact receipt. Four payloads become one paragraph.

Merge into issue_refund (Patterns 1 + 3). POST /refunds (#11) needs GET /payments/{id} (#10) to find what is refundable, and PUT /orders/{id} (#4) to move the order to refunded / partially_refunded. All three fuse into one guarded tool: unknown order, missing payment, and over-refund are refused with plain-language errors. Note what this implies for #4 as a standalone endpoint — see "dropped" below.

Merge into get_order_status (Patterns 1 + 2). GET /orders/{id} (#2), GET /invoices/{id} (#7), GET /payments/{id} (#10), and GET /refunds/{id} (#12) answer one question: "what is the state of this order?" The tool fans out, then prunes to a markdown brief — customer, total, paid, refunded, net. No audit columns cross the boundary.

Become resources (Pattern 3). GET /orders (#1) becomes enterprise://billing/orders — a cacheable, paginated index (Pattern 4: 25 per page, cursor-style page URIs). GET /invoices/{id} (#7) becomes the resource template enterprise://billing/invoices/{invoice_id} — a read the client can cache and re-fetch for free.

Dropped — PUT /orders/{id} (#4) as a standalone. Agents must not set arbitrary order statuses. Every legitimate status transition (confirmed → refunded, partially_refunded) happens inside place_order or issue_refund, where the guards live. A generic status setter is a state-machine violation with a JSON Schema.

Dropped — DELETE /orders/{id} (#5). Hard deletes are never an agent affordance. Cancellation flows through issue_refund, which voids the money and records the reason. The row stays for audit.

Dropped — GET /invoices (#6), the list. Agents navigate invoices through orders, not through the invoice table. A second unbounded list endpoint adds nothing that the paginated orders resource does not already give, and it would need its own Pattern 4 guard for zero benefit.

Twelve endpoints in, five agent affordances out. The mapping is total: every endpoint is merged, converted, or dropped for a stated reason.

The complete server. Downstream services are mocked with httpx.MockTransport — no network, fully runnable. Save as blueprint_server.py; run python blueprint_server.py to serve it over stdio, or import server to drive it in-process.

"""Module 3 blueprint: the legacy 12-endpoint 'Enterprise Order & Billing'
OpenAPI surface, redesigned into a curated 3-tool + 2-resource MCPServer.

Run:  python blueprint_server.py            # stdio MCP server
"""
import asyncio
import httpx
from mcp.server.mcpserver import MCPServer

# ------------------------------------------------------------ mock backend
CUSTOMERS = {"c-1": {"name": "Awanish Singh", "tier": "gold"},
             "c-2": {"name": "Priya Nair", "tier": "standard"}}
PRICES = {"KB-01": 89.99, "MS-07": 68.52}
STOCK = {"KB-01": 140, "MS-07": 12}
ORDERS: dict[str, dict] = {}
INVOICES: dict[str, dict] = {}
PAYMENTS: dict[str, dict] = {}
REFUNDS: dict[str, dict] = {}

def mock_handler(request: httpx.Request) -> httpx.Response:
    import json
    p, m = request.url.path, request.method
    seg = p.strip("/").split("/")
    if m == "GET" and p == "/stock":
        sku = request.url.params["sku"]
        return httpx.Response(200, json={"sku": sku, "on_hand": STOCK.get(sku, 0)})
    if m == "POST" and p == "/orders":
        body = json.loads(request.content)
        oid = f"o-{len(ORDERS) + 9001}"
        ORDERS[oid] = {"order_id": oid, "customer_id": body["customer_id"],
                       "items": body["items"], "total": body["total"],
                       "status": "confirmed"}
        for it in body["items"]:
            STOCK[it["sku"]] -= it["qty"]
        return httpx.Response(201, json=ORDERS[oid])
    if m == "GET" and p == "/orders":
        page = int(request.url.params.get("page", 1))
        ids = sorted(ORDERS)[(page - 1) * 25: page * 25]
        return httpx.Response(200, json={"orders": [ORDERS[i] for i in ids],
                                         "page": page,
                                         "has_more": len(ORDERS) > page * 25})
    if m == "GET" and len(seg) == 2 and seg[0] == "orders":
        o = ORDERS.get(seg[1])
        return httpx.Response(200, json=o) if o else httpx.Response(404)
    if m == "PUT" and len(seg) == 2 and seg[0] == "orders":
        o = ORDERS[seg[1]]
        o["status"] = json.loads(request.content)["status"]
        return httpx.Response(200, json=o)
    if m == "POST" and p == "/invoices":
        body = json.loads(request.content)
        iid = f"inv-{len(INVOICES) + 5001}"
        INVOICES[iid] = {"invoice_id": iid, "order_id": body["order_id"],
                         "amount": body["amount"], "status": "issued"}
        return httpx.Response(201, json=INVOICES[iid])
    if m == "GET" and len(seg) == 2 and seg[0] == "invoices":
        inv = INVOICES.get(seg[1])
        return httpx.Response(200, json=inv) if inv else httpx.Response(404)
    if m == "POST" and p == "/payments":
        body = json.loads(request.content)
        pid = f"pay-{len(PAYMENTS) + 7001}"
        PAYMENTS[pid] = {"payment_id": pid, "order_id": body["order_id"],
                         "amount": body["amount"], "status": "captured"}
        return httpx.Response(201, json=PAYMENTS[pid])
    if m == "GET" and p == "/payments":
        oid = request.url.params["order_id"]
        found = [x for x in PAYMENTS.values() if x["order_id"] == oid]
        return httpx.Response(200, json={"payments": found})
    if m == "POST" and p == "/refunds":
        body = json.loads(request.content)
        rid = f"rfnd-{len(REFUNDS) + 3001}"
        REFUNDS[rid] = {"refund_id": rid, "payment_id": body["payment_id"],
                        "amount": body["amount"], "reason": body["reason"],
                        "status": "issued"}
        return httpx.Response(201, json=REFUNDS[rid])
    if m == "GET" and p == "/refunds":
        oid = request.url.params["order_id"]
        pay_ids = {x["payment_id"] for x in PAYMENTS.values()
                   if x["order_id"] == oid}
        return httpx.Response(200, json={"refunds": [r for r in REFUNDS.values()
                                                     if r["payment_id"] in pay_ids]})
    return httpx.Response(404, json={"error": "unknown route"})

TRANSPORT = httpx.MockTransport(mock_handler)

# ------------------------------------------------------------ MCP surface
server = MCPServer("order-billing-mcp", version="1.0.0")

@server.tool()
async def place_order(customer_id: str, items: list[dict]) -> str:
    """Intent: take this customer's money for these items.

    Merges POST /orders + POST /invoices + POST /payments. Validates the
    customer, checks stock, then creates order, invoice and payment as one
    atomic-feeling business step. Returns a compact receipt, not four payloads.
    """
    if customer_id not in CUSTOMERS:
        return f"error: unknown customer {customer_id}"
    async with httpx.AsyncClient(transport=TRANSPORT, base_url="http://svc") as c:
        for it in items:  # stock check before any write
            s = (await c.get("/stock", params={"sku": it["sku"]})).json()
            if s["on_hand"] < it["qty"]:
                return (f"error: insufficient stock for {it['sku']} "
                        f"(need {it['qty']}, have {s['on_hand']})")
        total = round(sum(PRICES[it["sku"]] * it["qty"] for it in items), 2)
        order = (await c.post("/orders", json={"customer_id": customer_id,
                                               "items": items,
                                               "total": total})).json()
        invoice = (await c.post("/invoices", json={"order_id": order["order_id"],
                                                   "amount": total})).json()
        payment = (await c.post("/payments", json={"order_id": order["order_id"],
                                                   "amount": total})).json()
    cust = CUSTOMERS[customer_id]
    return "\n".join([
        f"# Order {order['order_id']} confirmed",
        f"Customer: {cust['name']} ({cust['tier']})",
        f"Items: {', '.join(it['sku'] + ' × ' + str(it['qty']) for it in items)}",
        f"Total: ${total:.2f} — invoice {invoice['invoice_id']}, "
        f"payment {payment['payment_id']} ({payment['status']})"])

@server.tool()
async def get_order_status(order_id: str) -> str:
    """Intent: 'what is the state of this order, financially and logistically?'

    Merges GET /orders/{id} + GET /invoices/{id} + GET /payments/{id} +
    GET /refunds/{id} into one pruned markdown brief. No audit columns, no UUIDs.
    """
    async with httpx.AsyncClient(transport=TRANSPORT, base_url="http://svc") as c:
        r = await c.get(f"/orders/{order_id}")
        if r.status_code == 404:
            return f"error: unknown order {order_id}"
        order = r.json()
        payments = (await c.get("/payments",
                                params={"order_id": order_id})).json()["payments"]
        refunds = (await c.get("/refunds",
                               params={"order_id": order_id})).json()["refunds"]
    cust = CUSTOMERS[order["customer_id"]]["name"]
    paid = sum(p["amount"] for p in payments)
    refunded = sum(x["amount"] for x in refunds)
    lines = [f"# Order {order_id} — {order['status']}",
             f"Customer: {cust} · Total: ${order['total']:.2f}",
             f"Paid: ${paid:.2f} · Refunded: ${refunded:.2f} · "
             f"Net: ${paid - refunded:.2f}"]
    if refunds:
        lines.append("Refunds: " + ", ".join(
            f"{x['refund_id']} ${x['amount']:.2f} ({x['reason']})" for x in refunds))
    return "\n".join(lines)

@server.tool()
async def issue_refund(order_id: str, amount: float, reason: str) -> str:
    """Intent: give money back for this order.

    Merges GET /payments/{id} (lookup) + POST /refunds + PUT /orders/{id}
    (status transition). Blast-radius guards: unknown order, no payment,
    and over-refund are all refused with plain-language errors.
    """
    async with httpx.AsyncClient(transport=TRANSPORT, base_url="http://svc") as c:
        if (await c.get(f"/orders/{order_id}")).status_code == 404:
            return f"error: unknown order {order_id}"
        payments = (await c.get("/payments",
                                params={"order_id": order_id})).json()["payments"]
        if not payments:
            return f"error: order {order_id} has no captured payment to refund against"
        payment = payments[0]
        already = sum(x["amount"] for x in
                      (await c.get("/refunds",
                                   params={"order_id": order_id})).json()["refunds"])
        if amount > payment["amount"] - already:
            return (f"error: refund ${amount:.2f} exceeds refundable "
                    f"${payment['amount'] - already:.2f}")
        refund = (await c.post("/refunds", json={"payment_id": payment["payment_id"],
                                                  "amount": amount,
                                                  "reason": reason})).json()
        new_status = ("refunded" if amount + already >= payment["amount"]
                      else "partially_refunded")
        await c.put(f"/orders/{order_id}", json={"status": new_status})
    return (f"Refund {refund['refund_id']}: ${amount:.2f} back to order {order_id} "
            f"({reason}). Order status → {new_status}.")

@server.resource("enterprise://billing/orders")
async def orders_index() -> str:
    """Paginated order index (page 1). GET /orders, but as a cacheable read."""
    async with httpx.AsyncClient(transport=TRANSPORT, base_url="http://svc") as c:
        page = (await c.get("/orders", params={"page": 1})).json()
    lines = ["# Orders — page 1"]
    lines += [f"- {o['order_id']}: ${o['total']:.2f} · {o['status']}"
              for o in page["orders"]]
    if page["has_more"]:
        lines.append("Next: enterprise://billing/orders/pages/2")
    return "\n".join(lines)

@server.resource("enterprise://billing/orders/pages/{page}")
async def orders_page(page: str) -> str:
    async with httpx.AsyncClient(transport=TRANSPORT, base_url="http://svc") as c:
        data = (await c.get("/orders", params={"page": int(page)})).json()
    lines = [f"# Orders — page {page}"]
    lines += [f"- {o['order_id']}: ${o['total']:.2f} · {o['status']}"
              for o in data["orders"]]
    if data["has_more"]:
        lines.append(f"Next: enterprise://billing/orders/pages/{int(page) + 1}")
    return "\n".join(lines)

@server.resource("enterprise://billing/invoices/{invoice_id}")
async def invoice_detail(invoice_id: str) -> str:
    """GET /invoices/{id} as a read resource: safe to cache and re-read."""
    async with httpx.AsyncClient(transport=TRANSPORT, base_url="http://svc") as c:
        r = await c.get(f"/invoices/{invoice_id}")
    if r.status_code == 404:
        return f"error: unknown invoice {invoice_id}"
    inv = r.json()
    return (f"# Invoice {inv['invoice_id']}\nOrder: {inv['order_id']}\n"
            f"Amount: ${inv['amount']:.2f}\nStatus: {inv['status']}")

if __name__ == "__main__":
    server.run(transport="stdio")

End-to-end verification. The full lifecycle was executed two ways: tools invoked in-process, and a real ClientSession over stdio_client against the server as a subprocess (negotiated protocol 2025-11-25). Transcript:

tools: ['get_order_status', 'issue_refund', 'place_order']
# Order o-9001 confirmed
Customer: Awanish Singh (gold)
Items: KB-01 × 2, MS-07 × 1
Total: $248.50 — invoice inv-5001, payment pay-7001 (captured)
# Order o-9001 — confirmed
Customer: Awanish Singh · Total: $248.50
Paid: $248.50 · Refunded: $0.00 · Net: $248.50
Refund rfnd-3001: $68.52 back to order o-9001 (mouse returned). Order status → partially_refunded.
in-process E2E green
negotiated protocol: 2025-11-25
stdio wire green: full place_order -> status -> resource round trip

Notice the shape of the win. The agent's entire order lifecycle — place, inspect, partially refund, re-inspect — took four tool calls, each returning a paragraph. Against the raw 12-endpoint surface the same lifecycle is ten or more calls with UUID correlation between them. The catalog the model sees has three tools, not twelve endpoints. That is the conversion.

3.8 What to do on Monday

If you take one page from this module into your next design review, make it this sequence:

  1. Inventory the domain's intents, not its endpoints. Ask the product team what agents will actually do — usually five to ten intents per domain. Those are your tools.
  2. Aggregate first. One intent, one tool, asyncio.gather underneath. Hide the join keys in Python.
  3. Prune at the boundary. Define the agent-facing shape as a Pydantic model. Measure the token delta. If you cannot show a 70%+ reduction on entity reads, you have not pruned.
  4. Split reads from writes. GETs become resources (cached, subscribable); mutating verbs become guarded tools. Every write gets its blast-radius check inside the tool, not in the prompt.
  5. Cap every list. Page size clamped server-side, aggregates computed server-side, pointers instead of dumps. No exceptions, including the endpoint "nobody will ever call with that much data."
  6. Delete the affordances agents should not have. Hard deletes, arbitrary status setters, and unbounded list endpoints do not survive the conversion. Say why, in the design doc, per endpoint — the table in §3.7 is the template.

The generator will still be tempting on a Friday afternoon. Run the math from §3.1 first: 80,000 tokens of catalog, collapsing tool selection, 8–12 round-trips per workflow, and your audit columns in the model's hands. Then build the facade. Your agents — and your context windows — will feel the difference on Monday morning.

Module 4 — Production Python MCP Server & Client Implementation

In plain language: A working demo is only the start. This module shows how to build a Python bridge that checks inputs and access, reuses connections, retries safely, and returns errors people can act on.

So far this guide has treated MCP as a protocol: messages, capabilities, versions. This module treats it as a running system. You will build one MCP server the way an enterprise would run it: pooled connections, strict timeouts, retries with backoff, validated inputs, and errors the model can act on. You will also build one client that talks to it over Streamable HTTP, with auth, caching, and timeout guards.

Every line of code in this module executed green. The server and client live as real files at code/module-4/ in the build tree, and the chapter embeds them in full. Nothing is sketched. When a claim appears about runtime behavior, a test asserts it.

4.1 What "production" means for an MCP server

A demo MCP server wraps a function and returns a string. A production one sits between an agent loop and real downstream services, and that position creates obligations a demo never feels.

First, concurrency. An agent fires many tool calls per task, and many agents share one server. If each tool call builds its own HTTP client, each call pays a fresh TCP and TLS handshake, connection pools never warm up, and socket counts grow with concurrency until something breaks. The fix is one shared client with a bounded pool, created once and closed once.

Second, failure. Downstream services time out, return 500s, and reject bad input. The agent must never see a raw traceback or deliberate over whether to retry a 503. The server translates every failure into one of two shapes: a result, or an isError tool result carrying recovery instructions the model can follow without thinking.

Third, input quality. The model's only documentation for a tool is the JSON Schema the server publishes. Vague schemas produce vague arguments, which produce downstream 400s. Precise schemas — patterns, ranges, descriptions written for the reader that is an LLM — move validation to the cheapest possible place: before any network call happens.

This module builds all three: lifespan-managed pooling, server-side retries, two-layer validation, and translated errors. Then it builds the client that deserves such a server.

4.2 SDK 2.x ground truth: the renames

This module uses MCP SDK 2.3.0, and 2.x renamed several 1.x APIs you will still see in older tutorials. The renames that matter here:

1.x name 2.x name Where it appears
FastMCP MCPServer (mcp.server.mcpserver) Server class, server.tool(), server.resource()
streamablehttp_client streamable_http_client (mcp.client.streamable_http) Client transport
McpError MCPError (mcp.shared.exceptions) Client-side error type
inputSchema attribute input_schema attribute (inputSchema remains the wire alias) Tool objects

Two versions matter here. The initialize handshake in this module negotiates the legacy version 2025-11-25. The modern version is 2026-07-28; it has no initialize handshake. A client may use server/discover to learn the server’s supported versions and capabilities, but that call is optional. Capstone 2 uses the modern format for live subscriptions. Check the version used by your actual connection.

4.3 The system we are building

One MCPServer named orders-billing-mcp fronts two downstream microservices: an OrderService and a BillingService. The service boundary is deliberate. In a real enterprise the agent never talks to microservices directly. The MCP server is the integration point. So it owns three policies in one place: HTTP (pooling, timeouts, retries), validation, and error translation.

The server exposes three tools and one resource:

  • get_order_summary — read an order, optionally with line items, from the OrderService. Reports staged progress.
  • issue_refund — post a refund to the BillingService, guarded by an idempotency key.
  • update_billing_address — patch a customer's address in the BillingService.
  • billing://invoices/{invoice_id} — a resource template serving invoice documents.

The client connects over Streamable HTTP with a bearer token, caches the tool list, converts tool schemas to provider-neutral LLM function definitions, and calls tools behind two timeout guards while consuming progress notifications.

For tests, the downstream services are scripted with httpx.MockTransport. No network, no Docker, deterministic failures.

4.4 Lifespan: one pooled client for the server's whole life

An MCP server process lives for weeks. Its downstream HTTP client should live exactly as long — no longer, no shorter. The SDK's lifespan hook (@asynccontextmanager, passed as lifespan= to MCPServer) exists for precisely this: build expensive shared state once at startup, hand it to every request through ctx.request_context.lifespan_context, and tear it down once at shutdown.

The alternative — a client per tool call — is the most common production bug in MCP servers. It looks harmless in a demo. Under load it means thousands of short-lived connection pools, no keep-alive reuse, and file-descriptor exhaustion that arrives at 3 AM.

Two details in the code deserve attention. Timeouts are per-phase (connect, read, write, pool), not one vague number. A hung TLS handshake and a hung response body are different failures with different budgets; a single timeout conflates them. And the pooling limits are set on the real httpx.AsyncHTTPTransport, because that is where the connection pool lives — passing limits= to httpx.AsyncClient only works when the client builds its own default transport.

The module header and lifespan (the configuration constants they read open the listing in §4.5):

"""Enterprise MCP server: one MCPServer fronting OrderService + BillingService.

Architecture decisions worth knowing before you read the code:

1. ONE shared httpx.AsyncClient lives for the whole server lifetime (built in the
   lifespan, closed on shutdown). Every tool reuses it through
   ``ctx.request_context.lifespan_context["http"]``. A client per tool call would
   mean a fresh TCP/TLS handshake pool per call and unbounded sockets under load.

2. Retries live in the MCP server (RetryTransport), NOT in the agent. The agent
   should see one clean result or one actionable error — never "try again, maybe".
   Retrying POSTs is safe here only because every mutating call carries an
   Idempotency-Key (see issue_refund).

3. Validation happens twice, for two audiences: the tool signature's
   ``Annotated[..., Field(...)]`` becomes the JSON Schema the LLM reads (fast,
   local feedback for typos); the Pydantic models inside enforce cross-field
   rules (audit rules the schema language cannot express).

4. Downstream failures become ``ToolError`` with remediation text the LLM can act
   on. Raw tracebacks never reach the model: anticipated failures raise
   ``ToolError`` (``isError: true``, logged at INFO, no traceback); anything
   uncaught is converted by the SDK into a generic "Error executing tool <name>"
   so internals never leak.

Run with the scripted mock downstream (tests / local dev)::

    MCP_USE_MOCK_DOWNSTREAM=1 python -m enterprise_server   # serves Streamable HTTP on :8000

Point at the real services by leaving the env var unset and setting
ORDER_SERVICE_BASE_URL / BILLING_SERVICE_BASE_URL.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import asyncio
import json
import logging
import os
import random
import re
from contextlib import asynccontextmanager
from decimal import Decimal
from typing import Annotated, Any, Awaitable, Callable
from uuid import uuid4

import httpx
from pydantic import BaseModel, Field, ValidationError, field_validator, model_validator

from mcp.server.mcpserver import Context, MCPServer
from mcp.server.mcpserver.exceptions import ResourceNotFoundError, ToolError

logger = logging.getLogger("orders-billing-mcp")
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Lifespan: build ONE pooled client, share it, close it on shutdown.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
def _downstream_transport() -> httpx.AsyncBaseTransport:
    """Production transport: pooled connections + retry policy."""
    inner = httpx.AsyncHTTPTransport(
        limits=httpx.Limits(
            max_connections=MAX_CONNECTIONS,
            max_keepalive_connections=MAX_KEEPALIVE_CONNECTIONS,
        )
    )
    return RetryTransport(inner, max_attempts=RETRY_MAX_ATTEMPTS, base_delay=RETRY_BASE_DELAY)


@asynccontextmanager
async def app_lifespan(server: MCPServer):  # noqa: ARG001 - signature fixed by SDK
    """Create the single shared httpx.AsyncClient; close it on shutdown.

    Why one client: connection pooling only works if connections are reused.
    A client per request (or per tool call) defeats keep-alive, pays a fresh
    TCP+TLS handshake per call, and lets socket count grow with concurrency.
    The lifespan is the SDK's hook for exactly this: setup once, share via
    ``ctx.request_context.lifespan_context``, teardown once.
    """
    if os.environ.get("MCP_USE_MOCK_DOWNSTREAM") == "1":
        transport: httpx.AsyncBaseTransport = RetryTransport(
            httpx.MockTransport(_mock_downstream_handler),
            max_attempts=RETRY_MAX_ATTEMPTS,
            base_delay=RETRY_BASE_DELAY,
        )
    else:
        transport = _downstream_transport()
    timeout = httpx.Timeout(
        connect=CONNECT_TIMEOUT, read=READ_TIMEOUT, write=WRITE_TIMEOUT, pool=POOL_TIMEOUT
    )
    # Strict per-phase timeouts (not one vague number): a hung TLS handshake
    # and a hung response body are different failures with different budgets.
    client = httpx.AsyncClient(transport=transport, timeout=timeout)
    logger.info(
        "downstream HTTP client ready (pool %d conns / %d keep-alive)",
        MAX_CONNECTIONS, MAX_KEEPALIVE_CONNECTIONS,
    )
    try:
        yield {"http": client}
    finally:
        await client.aclose()
        logger.info("downstream HTTP client closed")


server = MCPServer("orders-billing-mcp", version="2.0.0", lifespan=app_lifespan)
# 1.x -> 2.x rename note: this class was called FastMCP in MCP SDK 1.x.
# In 2.x it is MCPServer (import from mcp.server.mcpserver). Same decorators.

4.5 Retries belong in the server, not the agent

Transient failures — a 503 during a deploy, a blip in the network — are infrastructure facts, not reasoning tasks. When retry logic lives in the agent loop, every agent reimplements backoff, usually badly, and the model burns tokens deliberating over failures it cannot fix. When it lives in the MCP server, there is one policy, applied uniformly to every tool, and the agent sees exactly two outcomes: a result, or one actionable error.

RetryTransport wraps any httpx.AsyncBaseTransport and retries 5xx statuses, timeouts, and network errors with exponential backoff and jitter. Two design decisions matter.

First, the last attempt's response is returned, not raised, so the tool layer can translate the status into a ToolError with recovery instructions. The last attempt's exception is re-raised for the same translation. The transport never invents error semantics; it only decides whether to try again.

Second, retrying POSTs is safe here only because every mutating call carries an Idempotency-Key (section 4.8). Blindly retrying non-idempotent POSTs is how double charges happen. The comment on the class says this plainly, because the next engineer to touch this code needs to see the precondition.

A subtle correctness point: on a retryable 5xx where attempts remain, the response is closed before backing off, returning its connection to the pool. Leaking a response per retry would drain the very pool the lifespan worked to build.

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Configuration. Module-level constants (not hidden in the lifespan body) so
# tests and operators can shrink or raise them in one place.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
ORDER_SERVICE_BASE_URL = os.environ.get(
    "ORDER_SERVICE_BASE_URL", "https://orders.internal.example.com"
)
BILLING_SERVICE_BASE_URL = os.environ.get(
    "BILLING_SERVICE_BASE_URL", "https://billing.internal.example.com"
)

MAX_CONNECTIONS = 100            # total pooled connections across all origins
MAX_KEEPALIVE_CONNECTIONS = 20   # idle keep-alive connections kept warm
CONNECT_TIMEOUT = 5.0            # TCP + TLS handshake budget
READ_TIMEOUT = 10.0              # time-to-first-byte / between-bytes budget
WRITE_TIMEOUT = 10.0             # request-body send budget
POOL_TIMEOUT = 5.0               # how long to wait for a free pooled connection
RETRY_MAX_ATTEMPTS = 3           # 1 initial try + 2 retries
RETRY_BASE_DELAY = 0.2           # first backoff; doubles each attempt, plus jitter

ORDER_ID_PATTERN = r"^ORD-\d{6}$"
SUPPORTED_CURRENCIES = {"USD", "EUR", "INR", "GBP"}


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Retry transport: exponential backoff + jitter around any inner transport.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
class RetryTransport(httpx.AsyncBaseTransport):
    """Retry transient downstream failures with exponential backoff.

    Retries ``5xx`` statuses, timeouts, and network errors. The *last* attempt's
    response is returned as-is (not raised) so the tool layer can translate the
    status into an actionable ``ToolError``. The last attempt's *exception*
    (timeout / network error) is re-raised for the same translation.

    Why here and not in the agent: the retry policy is an infrastructure
    concern. One policy, applied uniformly to every tool, keeps the agent's
    error surface small: it either gets a result or a single remediation
    message. Scattering ``try/except`` retry loops across agent code means
    N policies, N backoff bugs, and the LLM paying tokens to deliberate about
    transient 503s it cannot fix.
    """

    RETRYABLE_STATUS = frozenset({500, 502, 503, 504})
    RETRYABLE_EXC = (httpx.TimeoutException, httpx.NetworkError)

    def __init__(
        self,
        inner: httpx.AsyncBaseTransport,
        *,
        max_attempts: int = RETRY_MAX_ATTEMPTS,
        base_delay: float = RETRY_BASE_DELAY,
        max_delay: float = 5.0,
    ) -> None:
        self._inner = inner
        self._max_attempts = max_attempts
        self._base_delay = base_delay
        self._max_delay = max_delay
        self.attempts_made = 0  # observability hook for tests / metrics

    async def handle_async_request(self, request: httpx.Request) -> httpx.Response:
        for attempt in range(1, self._max_attempts + 1):
            self.attempts_made += 1
            try:
                response = await self._inner.handle_async_request(request)
            except self.RETRYABLE_EXC as exc:
                logger.warning(
                    "downstream %s %s failed (attempt %d/%d): %s",
                    request.method, request.url.path, attempt, self._max_attempts, exc,
                )
                if attempt == self._max_attempts:
                    raise
            else:
                if response.status_code not in self.RETRYABLE_STATUS or attempt == self._max_attempts:
                    return response
                # Retryable 5xx and attempts remain: drop this response so its
                # connection returns to the pool, then back off.
                logger.warning(
                    "downstream %s %s -> %d (attempt %d/%d); retrying",
                    request.method, request.url.path, response.status_code,
                    attempt, self._max_attempts,
                )
                await response.aclose()
            if attempt < self._max_attempts:
                delay = min(self._base_delay * 2 ** (attempt - 1), self._max_delay)
                await asyncio.sleep(delay * (0.5 + random.random()))  # jittered backoff
        raise AssertionError("unreachable: loop always returns or raises")

4.6 Validation in two layers, for two audiences

The model's only documentation for a tool is the JSON Schema the server publishes from the function signature. That makes Field(description=...) load-bearing documentation, not decoration. A description like "Order identifier, e.g. ORD-004213" is read by the LLM at call time; a missing description leaves the model guessing, and guessing produces downstream 404s.

So validation happens twice, for two audiences. The signature's Annotated[..., Field(...)] constraints — patterns, ranges, lengths — become the JSON Schema the model reads. This is the fast layer: a typo fails locally, before any network call, with the expected shape spelled out. Behind it sit Pydantic v2 models enforcing rules the schema language cannot express. The example in this module is a cross-field audit rule: refunds over 1000 require a reason of at least 30 characters. JSON Schema cannot say "the minimum length of this field depends on the value of that field." A @model_validator(mode="after") can.

Here is an excerpt of what the SDK actually publishes for issue_refund — captured from a live list_tools() call, not hand-written (amount, reason, and currency properties omitted for space):

{
  "properties": {
    "order_id": {
      "description": "Order identifier, e.g. ORD-004213.",
      "pattern": "^ORD-\\d{6}$",
      "title": "Order Id",
      "type": "string"
    },
    "idempotency_key": {
      "anyOf": [
        {"maxLength": 64, "minLength": 8, "type": "string"},
        {"type": "null"}
      ],
      "default": null,
      "description": "Unique key for this refund. Reuse the SAME key when retrying — a new key would create a second refund. Generated automatically when omitted.",
      "title": "Idempotency Key"
    }
  },
  "required": ["order_id", "amount", "reason"],
  "type": "object",
  "title": "issue_refundArguments"
}

Note what is absent: the injected ctx parameter never appears in the schema. The SDK detects the Context annotation and excludes it. A test asserts this, because a ctx leaking into the tool schema would invite the model to invent a value for it.

The models:

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Pydantic v2 models: Field descriptions become the LLM's documentation.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
class OrderId(BaseModel):
    order_id: str = Field(
        pattern=ORDER_ID_PATTERN,
        description=(
            "Order identifier, e.g. ORD-004213. The pattern is checked locally, "
            "before any network call, so a typo fails fast with a precise message "
            "instead of a confusing downstream 404."
        ),
    )


class Money(BaseModel):
    amount: Decimal = Field(
        gt=0,
        le=Decimal("1000000"),
        max_digits=12,
        decimal_places=2,
        description="Refund amount in major currency units, e.g. 42.50. Must be positive.",
    )
    currency: str = Field(
        default="USD",
        pattern=r"^[A-Z]{3}$",
        description="ISO 4217 currency code, e.g. USD, EUR, INR, GBP.",
    )

    @field_validator("currency")
    @classmethod
    def _supported_currency(cls, v: str) -> str:
        if v not in SUPPORTED_CURRENCIES:
            raise ValueError(
                f"unsupported currency {v!r}; supported: {', '.join(sorted(SUPPORTED_CURRENCIES))}"
            )
        return v


class RefundRequest(BaseModel):
    order_id: str = Field(
        pattern=ORDER_ID_PATTERN,
        description="Order identifier, e.g. ORD-004213. Checked locally before any network call.",
    )
    money: Money = Field(description="How much to refund and in which currency.")
    reason: str = Field(
        min_length=10,
        max_length=500,
        description=(
            "Human-readable reason, 10-500 characters. Appears on the refund record "
            "and the customer receipt — write it for the customer, not the log."
        ),
    )
    idempotency_key: str = Field(
        min_length=8,
        max_length=64,
        description=(
            "Client-generated unique key for this refund (uuid4 hex is fine). The "
            "billing service stores it: retrying with the SAME key returns the "
            "original refund instead of creating a second one. Always reuse the "
            "key when retrying; never invent a new one for the same refund."
        ),
    )

    @field_validator("reason")
    @classmethod
    def _no_placeholder_reason(cls, v: str) -> str:
        if v.strip().lower() in {"test", "testing", "asdf", "placeholder"}:
            raise ValueError("reason looks like a placeholder; describe the actual refund reason")
        return v.strip()

    @model_validator(mode="after")
    def _large_refund_needs_detail(self) -> "RefundRequest":
        # Cross-field rule the JSON Schema language cannot express: the reason
        # length depends on the amount. This is why a Pydantic model sits
        # behind the tool, not just Annotated constraints on the signature.
        if self.money.amount > 1000 and len(self.reason) < 30:
            raise ValueError(
                "refunds over 1000 require a reason of at least 30 characters (audit rule)"
            )
        return self


class Address(BaseModel):
    street: str = Field(min_length=5, max_length=120, description="Street address with house/apartment number.")
    city: str = Field(min_length=2, max_length=80, description="City.")
    postal_code: str = Field(min_length=3, max_length=12, description="Postal/ZIP code.")
    country: str = Field(
        default="US",
        pattern=r"^[A-Z]{2}$",
        description="ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country code, e.g. US, IN.",
    )

    @model_validator(mode="after")
    def _postal_matches_country(self) -> "Address":
        if self.country == "US" and not re.fullmatch(r"\d{5}(-\d{4})?", self.postal_code):
            raise ValueError("US postal_code must be a ZIP like 10001 or 10001-1234")
        if self.country == "IN" and not re.fullmatch(r"\d{6}", self.postal_code):
            raise ValueError("IN postal_code must be a 6-digit PIN like 400001")
        return self

4.7 Errors the model can act on

When a downstream call fails, the model needs three things: what happened in plain language, what was or was not committed, and exactly what to do next. translate_downstream_error maps every httpx failure to a ToolError carrying that triple. ToolError is the SDK's contract for anticipated failures: the call returns isError: true with the message in content, and the server logs at INFO without a traceback. Anything uncaught is converted by the SDK into a generic Error executing tool <name> — no traceback, no hostnames, no internals leak to the model. The full traceback stays in the server log via logger.exception.

The mapping, in full. The SDK prefixes each message with Error executing tool <name>: , and it rejects schema violations (an order_id that misses the pattern) itself, before the wrapper runs:

Downstream signal What the model receives (isError: true) Recovery instruction Committed?
httpx.TimeoutException after retries "issue_refund timed out: the downstream service did not respond within 10s after 3 attempts" Retry the exact call once; if it fails again, tell the user the service is slow and stop Nothing — safe to retry
HTTP 404 "order ORD-000001 does not exist (downstream 404). Check the order ID — it must look like ORD-004213" Do not retry the same ID; ask the user to confirm it Nothing
HTTP 409 "rejected as a duplicate: a refund with this idempotency key was already processed" Do NOT retry — fetch the existing refund Already committed by the first call
HTTP 422 "rejected the input: postal_code 'BAD' is not valid for country US" Fix the highlighted field; call again Nothing
HTTP 5xx after retries "returned 503 after 3 attempts with backoff. The operation may or may not have committed" Refunds: retry with the SAME idempotency key; reads: retry the call Unknown — the idempotency key makes retry safe
Local ValidationError "Invalid arguments for issue_refund — nothing was sent downstream. Fix these and call again: Value error, refunds over 1000 require a reason of at least 30 characters (audit rule)" Fix the inputs; call again Nothing — no request was sent
Unexpected exception Generic "Error executing tool <name>" (SDK-generated) Report to the user; suggest support Unknown — do not retry blindly

Resources play by a different rule, and the difference matters. A missing invoice is not a tool failure — it is a protocol-level "no such resource," reported as JSON-RPC -32602 (invalid params) per SEP-2164 via ResourceNotFoundError. That lets clients distinguish "the invoice doesn't exist" from "the tool crashed," which an isError result cannot do.

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Error translation: httpx failures -> actionable LLM recovery instructions.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
def _safe_detail(response: httpx.Response) -> str:
    """Pull a short human message out of a downstream error body, capped."""
    try:
        body = response.json()
    except ValueError:
        body = {}
    if isinstance(body, dict):
        for key in ("detail", "error", "message"):
            if body.get(key):
                return str(body[key])[:200]
    return f"HTTP {response.status_code}"


def _format_validation_error(tool_name: str, exc: ValidationError) -> str:
    parts = [
        f"{'.'.join(str(p) for p in e['loc'])}: {e['msg']}" if e["loc"] else e["msg"]
        for e in exc.errors()
    ]
    return (
        f"Invalid arguments for {tool_name} — nothing was sent downstream. "
        "Fix these and call again: " + "; ".join(parts)
    )


def translate_downstream_error(
    exc: Exception, *, operation: str, order_id: str | None = None
) -> ToolError:
    """Map httpx failures to ToolError carrying LLM recovery instructions.

    The contract: every branch tells the model (1) what happened in plain
    language, (2) what was or was not committed, and (3) exactly what to do
    next — retry, fix input, or stop and escalate. No tracebacks, no URLs, no
    internal hostnames.
    """
    if isinstance(exc, httpx.TimeoutException):
        return ToolError(
            f"{operation} timed out: the downstream service did not respond within "
            f"{READ_TIMEOUT:g}s after {RETRY_MAX_ATTEMPTS} attempts with backoff. "
            "Nothing was committed — it is safe to retry this exact call once. "
            "If it times out again, do NOT keep retrying: tell the user the service "
            "is slow and suggest trying again in a few minutes."
        )
    if isinstance(exc, httpx.HTTPStatusError):
        status = exc.response.status_code
        if status == 404:
            return ToolError(
                f"{operation} failed: order {order_id or 'given'} does not exist "
                "(downstream 404). Check the order ID — it must look like ORD-004213. "
                "Do not retry the same ID; ask the user to confirm it."
            )
        if status == 409:
            return ToolError(
                f"{operation} rejected as a duplicate (downstream 409): a refund with "
                "this idempotency key was already processed. Do NOT retry — fetch the "
                "existing refund with get_order_summary instead."
            )
        if status == 422:
            return ToolError(
                f"{operation} rejected the input (downstream 422): {_safe_detail(exc.response)}. "
                "Fix the highlighted field and call again."
            )
        if status >= 500:
            return ToolError(
                f"{operation} failed: the downstream service returned {status} after "
                f"{RETRY_MAX_ATTEMPTS} attempts with backoff. The operation may or may "
                "not have committed — for refunds, retry with the SAME idempotency key "
                "so a duplicate is impossible; for reads, just retry the call."
            )
        return ToolError(
            f"{operation} failed with downstream status {status}: {_safe_detail(exc.response)}"
        )
    # Deliberately not chaining the original exception: its message may contain
    # hostnames, paths, or credentials. The server log keeps the full traceback.
    logger.exception("unexpected downstream failure in %s", operation)
    return ToolError(
        f"{operation} failed unexpectedly. Do not retry blindly — report this "
        "to the user and suggest contacting support."
    )

4.8 Tools, the resource, and the injected Context

Each tool is split in two. The *_impl functions are pure async functions taking the shared httpx.AsyncClient — no MCP machinery, directly unit-testable. The @server.tool() wrappers are thin: validate arguments into Pydantic models (raising ToolError with a precise message on failure), pull the shared client from the lifespan context, and delegate.

The wrappers declare ctx: Context as their first parameter. The SDK injects it by annotation and excludes it from the input schema. Inside tools, ctx.report_progress streams staged progress notifications to the client — get_order_summary reports at 10% (fetching order), 60% (fetching line items), and 100% (done). Section 4.10 shows the client consuming them.

The implementations:

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Tool implementations: pure async functions taking the shared client.
# Kept separate from the @server.tool() wrappers so they are unit-testable
# without any MCP machinery.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
ProgressFn = Callable[[float, float | None, str | None], Awaitable[None]]


async def get_order_summary_impl(
    http: httpx.AsyncClient,
    order_id: str,
    include_line_items: bool = True,
    progress: ProgressFn | None = None,
) -> dict[str, Any]:
    if progress:
        await progress(0.1, 1.0, "fetching order")
    try:
        resp = await http.get(f"{ORDER_SERVICE_BASE_URL}/orders/{order_id}")
        resp.raise_for_status()
    except (httpx.TimeoutException, httpx.HTTPStatusError) as exc:
        raise translate_downstream_error(exc, operation="get_order_summary", order_id=order_id)
    order = resp.json()

    items: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
    if include_line_items:
        if progress:
            await progress(0.6, 1.0, "fetching line items")
        try:
            resp = await http.get(f"{ORDER_SERVICE_BASE_URL}/orders/{order_id}/items")
            resp.raise_for_status()
        except (httpx.TimeoutException, httpx.HTTPStatusError) as exc:
            raise translate_downstream_error(exc, operation="get_order_summary", order_id=order_id)
        items = resp.json()
    if progress:
        await progress(1.0, 1.0, "done")
    return {"order": order, "line_items": items}


async def issue_refund_impl(http: httpx.AsyncClient, req: RefundRequest) -> dict[str, Any]:
    # The Idempotency-Key header is what makes server-side retries (and agent
    # retries) safe: the billing service keys the refund on it, so a replayed
    # request returns the original refund instead of charging twice.
    try:
        resp = await http.post(
            f"{BILLING_SERVICE_BASE_URL}/billing/refunds",
            json={
                "order_id": req.order_id,
                "amount": str(req.money.amount),
                "currency": req.money.currency,
                "reason": req.reason,
            },
            headers={"Idempotency-Key": req.idempotency_key},
        )
        resp.raise_for_status()
    except (httpx.TimeoutException, httpx.HTTPStatusError) as exc:
        raise translate_downstream_error(exc, operation="issue_refund", order_id=req.order_id)
    body = resp.json()
    body["idempotency_key"] = req.idempotency_key
    return body


async def update_billing_address_impl(
    http: httpx.AsyncClient, customer_id: str, address: Address
) -> dict[str, Any]:
    try:
        resp = await http.patch(
            f"{BILLING_SERVICE_BASE_URL}/billing/customers/{customer_id}/address",
            json=address.model_dump(),
        )
        resp.raise_for_status()
    except (httpx.TimeoutException, httpx.HTTPStatusError) as exc:
        raise translate_downstream_error(exc, operation="update_billing_address")
    return resp.json()


async def read_invoice_impl(http: httpx.AsyncClient, invoice_id: str) -> str:
    try:
        resp = await http.get(f"{BILLING_SERVICE_BASE_URL}/billing/invoices/{invoice_id}")
        resp.raise_for_status()
    except httpx.HTTPStatusError as exc:
        if exc.response.status_code == 404:
            # Resources use exceptions, not isError: a missing resource is a
            # -32602 protocol error per SEP-2164, so clients can distinguish
            # "no such invoice" from "tool failed".
            raise ResourceNotFoundError(f"invoice {invoice_id} does not exist")
        raise translate_downstream_error(exc, operation="read_invoice")
    except httpx.TimeoutException as exc:
        raise translate_downstream_error(exc, operation="read_invoice")
    return resp.text

The wrappers and the resource:

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# MCP tool / resource wrappers: validate, grab the shared client, delegate.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
def _shared_client(ctx: Context) -> httpx.AsyncClient:
    return ctx.request_context.lifespan_context["http"]


@server.tool()
async def get_order_summary(
    ctx: Context,
    order_id: Annotated[
        str,
        Field(
            pattern=ORDER_ID_PATTERN,
            description=(
                "Order identifier, e.g. ORD-004213. Checked locally before any "
                "network call, so a typo fails fast with a precise message."
            ),
        ),
    ],
    include_line_items: Annotated[
        bool,
        Field(description="Also fetch line items (one extra downstream call). Set false for a quick status check."),
    ] = True,
) -> dict:
    """Fetch an order and optionally its line items from the Order service."""
    # ctx is injected by name/annotation and excluded from the input schema.
    try:
        OrderId(order_id=order_id)
    except ValidationError as e:
        raise ToolError(_format_validation_error("get_order_summary", e))
    return await get_order_summary_impl(
        _shared_client(ctx), order_id, include_line_items, progress=ctx.report_progress
    )


@server.tool()
async def issue_refund(
    ctx: Context,
    order_id: Annotated[
        str,
        Field(pattern=ORDER_ID_PATTERN, description="Order identifier, e.g. ORD-004213."),
    ],
    amount: Annotated[float, Field(gt=0, description="Refund amount in major currency units, e.g. 42.50.")],
    reason: Annotated[
        str,
        Field(
            min_length=10,
            max_length=500,
            description="Human-readable reason for the customer receipt (10-500 chars).",
        ),
    ],
    currency: Annotated[
        str,
        Field(default="USD", pattern=r"^[A-Z]{3}$", description="ISO 4217 code: USD, EUR, INR, GBP."),
    ] = "USD",
    idempotency_key: Annotated[
        str | None,
        Field(
            default=None,
            min_length=8,
            max_length=64,
            description=(
                "Unique key for this refund. Reuse the SAME key when retrying — "
                "a new key would create a second refund. Generated automatically "
                "when omitted."
            ),
        ),
    ] = None,
) -> dict:
    """Issue a refund via the Billing service. Idempotent via idempotency_key."""
    try:
        req = RefundRequest(
            order_id=order_id,
            money=Money(amount=Decimal(str(amount)), currency=currency),
            reason=reason,
            idempotency_key=idempotency_key or f"refund-{uuid4().hex}",
        )
    except ValidationError as e:
        raise ToolError(_format_validation_error("issue_refund", e))
    return await issue_refund_impl(_shared_client(ctx), req)


@server.tool()
async def update_billing_address(
    ctx: Context,
    customer_id: Annotated[
        str,
        Field(pattern=r"^C-\d{3,}$", description="Customer identifier, e.g. C-100."),
    ],
    street: Annotated[str, Field(min_length=5, max_length=120, description="Street address with house/apartment number.")],
    city: Annotated[str, Field(min_length=2, max_length=80, description="City.")],
    postal_code: Annotated[str, Field(min_length=3, max_length=12, description="Postal/ZIP code.")],
    country: Annotated[
        str,
        Field(default="US", pattern=r"^[A-Z]{2}$", description="ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 code, e.g. US, IN."),
    ] = "US",
) -> dict:
    """Update a customer's billing address in the Billing service."""
    try:
        address = Address(street=street, city=city, postal_code=postal_code, country=country)
    except ValidationError as e:
        raise ToolError(_format_validation_error("update_billing_address", e))
    return await update_billing_address_impl(_shared_client(ctx), customer_id, address)


@server.resource("billing://invoices/{invoice_id}")
async def invoice_resource(
    invoice_id: str,
    ctx: Context,
) -> str:
    """Invoice document as JSON. Raises ResourceNotFoundError (-> -32602) when missing."""
    return await read_invoice_impl(_shared_client(ctx), invoice_id)

4.9 The scripted downstream: deterministic failure injection

Tests need downstream failures on demand: a 500 followed by a 200, a hung service, a duplicate idempotency key. httpx.MockTransport replaces the network, and MOCK_SCRIPT steers it per test — a mapping from "METHOD /path" to a list of scripted steps (("respond", status, body), ("sleep", seconds), ("raise", "timeout")). Steps are consumed in order, so "500 then success" is two list entries. Unscripted paths fall through to sensible default fixtures.

One honest test-harness note: MockTransport bypasses httpcore, which is where httpx normally enforces read timeouts. A ("sleep", 30) step would therefore sleep the full 30 seconds instead of raising httpx.ReadTimeout. The timeout test wraps the mock in a small TimeoutEnforcingTransport that restores production behavior with asyncio.wait_for. That wrapper lives in the test file, not the server — it is scaffolding, and it is labeled as such.

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Scripted mock downstream (tests / local dev). Tests steer it through
# MOCK_SCRIPT: "METHOD /path" -> list of steps, each ("respond", status, body),
# ("sleep", seconds), or ("raise", "timeout").
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
MOCK_SCRIPT: dict[str, list[tuple]] = {}

_MOCK_ORDERS = {
    "ORD-000001": {
        "order_id": "ORD-000001", "customer_id": "C-100",
        "status": "paid", "total": "189.99", "currency": "USD",
    }
}
_MOCK_ITEMS = {
    "ORD-000001": [
        {"sku": "WIDGET-1", "qty": 2, "unit_price": "79.99"},
        {"sku": "GADGET-9", "qty": 1, "unit_price": "30.01"},
    ]
}
_MOCK_INVOICES = {
    "INV-9001": {
        "invoice_id": "INV-9001", "order_id": "ORD-000001",
        "amount": "189.99", "currency": "USD", "status": "paid",
    }
}


async def _mock_downstream_handler(request: httpx.Request) -> httpx.Response:
    key = f"{request.method} {request.url.path}"
    steps = MOCK_SCRIPT.get(key, [])
    if steps:
        action, *args = steps.pop(0)
        if action == "sleep":
            await asyncio.sleep(args[0])
            return httpx.Response(200, json={"ok": True})
        if action == "raise":
            raise {"timeout": httpx.ReadTimeout("mock read timeout")}[args[0]]
        if action == "respond":
            status, body = args
            return httpx.Response(status, json=body)

    path = request.url.path
    if request.method == "GET" and path.startswith("/orders/") and path.endswith("/items"):
        order_id = path.split("/")[2]
        if order_id in _MOCK_ITEMS:
            return httpx.Response(200, json=_MOCK_ITEMS[order_id])
        return httpx.Response(404, json={"error": "order not found"})
    if request.method == "GET" and path.startswith("/orders/"):
        order_id = path.split("/")[2]
        if order_id in _MOCK_ORDERS:
            return httpx.Response(200, json=_MOCK_ORDERS[order_id])
        return httpx.Response(404, json={"error": "order not found"})
    if request.method == "POST" and path == "/billing/refunds":
        if request.headers.get("Idempotency-Key") == "DUPLICATE-KEY":
            return httpx.Response(409, json={"error": "duplicate idempotency key"})
        payload = json.loads(request.content.decode() or "{}")
        return httpx.Response(200, json={
            "refund_id": "RF-7", "status": "processed",
            "amount": payload.get("amount"), "currency": payload.get("currency"),
        })
    if request.method == "PATCH" and path.startswith("/billing/customers/"):
        payload = json.loads(request.content.decode() or "{}")
        if payload.get("postal_code") == "BAD":
            return httpx.Response(422, json={"detail": "postal_code 'BAD' is not valid for country US"})
        return httpx.Response(200, json={"customer_id": path.split("/")[3], "address": payload})
    if request.method == "GET" and path.startswith("/billing/invoices/"):
        invoice_id = path.split("/")[3]
        if invoice_id in _MOCK_INVOICES:
            return httpx.Response(200, json=_MOCK_INVOICES[invoice_id])
        return httpx.Response(404, json={"error": "invoice not found"})
    return httpx.Response(404, json={"error": f"no mock for {key}"})


if __name__ == "__main__":
    # Serve Streamable HTTP. With MCP_USE_MOCK_DOWNSTREAM=1 this is a fully
    # local server you can poke with the enterprise client.
    logging.basicConfig(level=logging.INFO)
    server.run(transport="streamable-http")

4.10 The enterprise client

4.10.1 Connecting with bearer auth over Streamable HTTP

The client passes a pre-configured httpx2.AsyncClient carrying the Authorization: Bearer header into streamable_http_client. Two things to get right. First, import httpx2, not httpx — the SDK vendors its HTTP layer under that name, and the parameter is typed for it. Second, when you provide the client, you own its lifecycle: the SDK only manages clients it creates itself, so the async with around httpx2.AsyncClient is yours to write.

enterprise_session wraps the whole handshake: open the transport, open the ClientSession, run initialize, and yield (session, tool_cache). The initialize result carries the negotiated protocolVersion — this module's tests assert it is 2025-11-25 — and the server info.

"""Enterprise MCP client: Streamable HTTP + auth + tool caching + guarded calls.

Companion to enterprise_server.py. Run against a local mock-backed server::

    # terminal 1:  MCP_USE_MOCK_DOWNSTREAM=1 python -m enterprise_server   # :8000
    # terminal 2:  python -m enterprise_client

Covers the client-side production concerns:

1. Auth headers ride on a custom httpx2.AsyncClient handed to
   ``streamable_http_client`` (2.x name; 1.x called it ``streamablehttp_client``).
   The SDK vendor-prefixes its httpx as ``httpx2`` — import that, not ``httpx``,
   when constructing the client you pass in.
2. ``list_tools()`` results are cached with a TTL. ``tools/list_changed``
   notifications invalidate the cache via ``message_handler`` — otherwise a
   server deploy that adds a tool is invisible until the TTL expires.
3. MCP ``Tool.input_schema`` is converted to provider-neutral function-calling
   dicts. The converter is deliberately generic: OpenAI and Anthropic each need
   a one-line adapter over it, and neither adapter belongs in shared code.
4. ``call_tool`` gets two timeout guards: the SDK's own
   ``read_timeout_seconds`` plus an outer ``asyncio.wait_for``. Belt and
   braces: the inner guard is protocol-aware, the outer one protects against
   anything the transport layer fails to time out.
5. Server-pushed progress notifications are consumed through
   ``progress_callback`` — the client passes a ``progressToken`` in ``_meta``
   and the server's ``ctx.report_progress`` calls arrive as
   ``notifications/progress``.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import asyncio
import time
from contextlib import asynccontextmanager
from typing import Any, AsyncIterator, Callable

import httpx2
from mcp import ClientSession
from mcp.client.streamable_http import streamable_http_client
from mcp.types import Tool

DEFAULT_TOOL_CACHE_TTL = 60.0
DEFAULT_TOOL_TIMEOUT = 30.0
@asynccontextmanager
async def enterprise_session(
    url: str,
    bearer_token: str,
    cache: ToolCache | None = None,
) -> AsyncIterator[tuple[ClientSession, ToolCache]]:
    """Connect to a Streamable HTTP MCP server with bearer auth.

    Yields ``(session, tool_cache)``. The session is initialized; the cache is
    wired to ``message_handler`` so ``tools/list_changed`` invalidates it.
    """
    cache = cache or ToolCache()
    headers = {"Authorization": f"Bearer {bearer_token}"}

    async def _on_message(message: Any) -> None:
        await _handle_message(message, cache)

    async with httpx2.AsyncClient(headers=headers) as http_client:
        # 1.x -> 2.x rename note: this was streamablehttp_client (no underscores)
        # in SDK 1.x; 2.x spells it streamable_http_client.
        async with streamable_http_client(url, http_client=http_client) as (read, write):
            async with ClientSession(read, write, message_handler=_on_message) as session:
                init = await session.initialize()
                server_name = init.server_info.name if init.server_info else "?"
                print(f"connected: {server_name} (protocol {init.protocol_version})")
                yield session, cache

4.10.2 Caching the tool list, invalidating on change

list_tools() is a network round trip, and an agent loop calls tools dozens of times per task while the tool list changes only on server deploy. ToolCache caches for 60 seconds — and, crucially, it does not rely on the TTL alone. The session's message_handler watches for notifications/tools/list_changed and invalidates eagerly.
