7.9 Running it for real (Docker)

Run this on a Docker-equipped machine — not in a sandbox.

The same code runs as seven containers: three mock services, two MCP servers, the gateway, and Redis. One image, per-service commands:

FROM python:3.12-slim

WORKDIR /app

# Install the runtime dependencies before copying source for layer caching.
COPY pyproject.toml ./
RUN python -c "import tomllib; print('\n'.join(tomllib.load(open('pyproject.toml', 'rb'))['project']['dependencies']))" > requirements.txt \
    && pip install --no-cache-dir -r requirements.txt

COPY mock_services/ ./mock_services/
COPY mcp_servers/ ./mcp_servers/
COPY gateway/ ./gateway/
COPY host/ ./host/

# Each service picks its own entry point via the compose `command:`.
EXPOSE 8000 8101 8102 9001 9002 9003
# Capstone 1 — docker-compose topology.
#
# > Run this on a Docker-equipped machine — not in a sandbox.
#   `docker compose up --build`, then in another shell:
#     python host/agent.py --role tier2_supervisor
#     python host/agent.py --role tier1_support
#
# Ports: mock REST services 9001-9003, MCP servers 8101-8102, gateway 8000.

services:
  redis:
    image: redis:7-alpine
    ports:
      - "6379:6379"

  order-service:
    build: .
    command: uvicorn mock_services.order_service:app --host 0.0.0.0 --port 9001
    ports:
      - "9001:9001"

  billing-service:
    build: .
    command: uvicorn mock_services.billing_service:app --host 0.0.0.0 --port 9002
    ports:
      - "9002:9002"

  inventory-service:
    build: .
    command: uvicorn mock_services.inventory_service:app --host 0.0.0.0 --port 9003
    ports:
      - "9003:9003"

  commerce-mcp:
    build: .
    command: uvicorn mcp_servers.commerce_server:app --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8101
    ports:
      - "8101:8101"
    environment:
      ORDER_SERVICE_URL: http://order-service:9001
      INVENTORY_SERVICE_URL: http://inventory-service:9003
      MCP_DEBUG: "1" # dev-only identity introspection tool
    depends_on:
      - order-service
      - inventory-service

  finance-mcp:
    build: .
    command: uvicorn mcp_servers.finance_server:app --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8102
    ports:
      - "8102:8102"
    environment:
      BILLING_SERVICE_URL: http://billing-service:9002
      MCP_DEBUG: "1"
    depends_on:
      - billing-service

  gateway:
    build: .
    command: uvicorn gateway.app:app --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8000
    ports:
      - "8000:8000"
    environment:
      COMMERCE_MCP_URL: http://commerce-mcp:8101
      FINANCE_MCP_URL: http://finance-mcp:8102
      GATEWAY_REDIS_URL: redis://redis:6379/0 # prod-style shared rate limiting
      GATEWAY_RATE_LIMIT_MAX: "120"
    depends_on:
      - commerce-mcp
      - finance-mcp
      - redis
docker compose up --build
# in another shell:
python host/agent.py --role tier2_supervisor   # sees all four tools
python host/agent.py --role tier1_support       # refund tool hidden

7.10 Production hardening: what changes

The capstone is honest about its simplifications. Each of these is a real work item before this mesh touches production:

  • Identity. The gateway verifies JWTs against the IdP's JWKS (RS256), not a committed HS256 secret. Upstream servers verify the exchanged token's signature and scope instead of recording headers. The dev-only debug_last_obo tool disappears entirely.
  • Sessions. Gateway sessions move to Redis so any replica serves any client. Upstream MCP sessions get pooled per gateway worker instead of opened per request — the per-request handshake here is correct but wasteful.
  • Rate limiting. Already Redis-backed via GATEWAY_REDIS_URL; add per-tool cost weights (a refund costs more budget than a stock check) and return Retry-After on 429.
  • Reliability. The finance server's idempotency keys need a durable store (the billing ledger, not process memory). Retries across gateway restarts must reuse the same deterministic key — which the agent already does.
  • Observability. The JSON span logs become real OpenTelemetry spans exported to a collector; the traceparent header is already in place. Add an audit resource (enterprise://orders/{id}/audit-log) recording every money-moving call with its OBO subject.
  • Downstream clients. One shared httpx client per server lifespan with connection pooling, timeouts, and circuit breakers — the per-call client here keeps tests simple.

7.11 What to remember

  • Federation splits ownership: domains own tools, the gateway owns auth, RBAC, identity propagation, and rate limits.
  • RBAC filters discovery, not just calls. A role cannot attack what it cannot see.
  • ToolError and unknown tool names become isError results with remediation text. Write every error message for an agent to read.
  • Bare -> dict tools arrive as JSON text blobs. structured_output=True with Pydantic models gives real structuredContent — and validates downstream payloads at the boundary.
  • Idempotency keys make "retry the refund" safe. Check the key before moving money, and make the key deterministic per ticket.
  • This example uses the legacy protocol version 2025-11-25 and its initialize handshake. The modern version, 2026-07-28, has no such handshake; server/discover is an optional way to check supported versions and capabilities. Always check the version used by your actual connection.
  • Trace context is just a header. Propagate traceparent at every hop and one ID ties the whole resolution together.

Capstone 2 — Autonomous SRE & Incident Triage Platform

In plain language: The example follows a simulated incident: read logs and metrics, run checks, explain what looks wrong, and wait for a human approval before changing a deployment. The sampling portion is a legacy-compatibility lesson, not a pattern to choose for a new system.

8.1 Why this capstone exists

An agent that can read production telemetry will eventually want to change production. Reading is safe. Mutating is not. Most agent demos skip that distinction and hand the model a kubectl wrapper with a prayer.

This capstone refuses the prayer. It builds a full incident-triage system: an MCP server that watches logs and metrics, digs through 5,000 lines of stack traces, and probes the database, Redis, and Kafka. Then it stops cold at the one action that matters. The rollback does not execute on the agent's word. It executes on a human's cryptographic signature.

Three hard problems carry the chapter. First, live telemetry: the host must learn about new log lines the moment they land, without polling. Second, nested reasoning: the server must get an LLM-quality summary of a huge log without holding an LLM API key. Third, governed mutation: the human approval must be unforgeable by the agent, expiring, and single-use. Each problem maps to one MCP primitive — subscriptions, sampling, and tools with a cryptographic gate — and the chapter implements all three against SDK 2.x, executed green.

8.2 Architecture

Read the diagram as two loops around one gate. The inner loop is telemetry: the host calls tools, the server reads the mock observability plane, and resource updates stream back over subscriptions/listen. The orange loop is sampling: the server ships 5,000 raw log lines to the host's model and gets a diagnostic report back — reasoning happens one level up, where the human can see it. The gate is the HITL path: the server proposes a rollback, parks a challenge in Redis, and waits. The on-call approver mints an HMAC token out-of-band. Only then does the server touch the mock Kubernetes API.

8.3 SDK and protocol details for this chapter

This example uses two kinds of connection. The modern connection handles live subscriptions and the rest of the workflow. A second, legacy connection is used only for the sampling demonstration. Keeping that difference visible avoids a common protocol-version mistake.

SDK names. The code was tested with mcp 2.3.0. In SDK 2.x, the high-level server is MCPServer; 1.x examples call it FastMCP. The high-level mcp.Client can connect to a running server over HTTP or in-process for tests.

Modern connection. The 2026-07-28 protocol has no initialize handshake or session ID. Each request carries its own metadata. A client can use server/discover to learn supported versions and capabilities, but that call is optional in the protocol. The Python SDK’s automatic client mode normally probes first. This capstone uses the modern client for subscriptions/listen, where the server publishes changes to a stream the client opened.

Legacy connection. The legacy protocol starts with initialize and supports server-initiated requests. The sampling callback in this capstone uses that older path. The code opens a separate Client(..., mode="legacy") connection for the one sampling call, then returns to the modern client for subscriptions, diagnostics, and approval.

Important for new projects: The 2026-07-28 specification deprecates sampling. The old server-to-host sampling call cannot run on a modern connection. For a new system, keep model calls in the host and do not copy this legacy-only path without checking the current SDK guidance.

8.4 Dynamic resources and live subscriptions

Polling is how triage systems go stale. A host that re-reads the log tail every ten seconds learns about the incident ten seconds late, and burns quota doing it. MCP resources solve the addressing — logs://service/{name}/recent names the tail directly — and subscriptions solve the freshness.

The server registers three resource templates. Each is a plain function; the URI template binds the path parameter:

@server.resource("k8s://clusters/{cluster}/deployments")
def cluster_deployments(cluster: str) -> str: ...

@server.resource("logs://service/{name}/recent")
def service_logs(name: str) -> str: ...

@server.resource("cluster://{cluster}/metrics")
def cluster_metrics(cluster: str) -> str: ...

Templates are cheap. The interesting part is the push. A lifespan background task plays the role of a live production system: every tick it appends fresh synthetic error lines, jitters the metrics snapshot, and publishes a ResourceUpdated event per touched URI through the server's subscription bus:

await server._subscriptions.publish(ResourceUpdated(uri=uri))

That publish is the 2.x form of ctx.notify_resource_updated(uri) — the same bus, reached directly because a background task has no request context. Subscribers opened the stream with client.listen(...):

async with client.listen(
    resource_subscriptions=["logs://service/payments-api/recent"]
) as sub:
    async for event in sub:
        ...

Two details deserve attention. First, URI matching is exact. The test subscribes to logs://service/payments-api/recent, and the rotation publishes exactly that string. A near-miss like logs://service/payments/recent matches nothing and the test hangs — the SDK will not fuzzy-match for you. Second, the server also notifies through the legacy path in the simulate_incident_burst tool (ctx.session.send_resource_updated), so hosts stuck on the 2025-era wire still get their notifications/resources/updated. One tool, both eras.

8.5 Legacy sampling: the host supplies the model response

In the older sampling pattern, the server sends information to the host and asks the host’s model for a response. The server does not need the model provider’s API key. That can be useful when maintaining an older integration, but sampling is deprecated in the 2026-07-28 specification and server-initiated calls do not work on a modern connection.

summarize_incident_logs pulls 5,000 raw log lines — generated by a seeded PRNG, so every run sees the same incident — and wraps them in a strict prompt: four sections, no preamble. Then one call:

result = await ctx.session.create_message(
    messages=[SamplingMessage(
        role="user",
        content=TextContent(type="text", text=prompt))],
    max_tokens=1000,
    system_prompt="You are a terse SRE assistant. No preamble, just the report.",
)

The host handles the request through its sampling_callback. In the test, the callback is a predictable mock: it counts exception types in the log lines and returns a fixed report. The test checks that the callback ran once and received all 5,000 lines. In the full host example, this tool call uses a separate legacy connection. The subscription and diagnostic steps use the modern connection. A new application should usually call its model from the host directly instead of building on deprecated sampling.

8.6 Progress streaming: long diagnostics without spinners

run_distributed_diagnostic checks three providers — database connection pool, Redis slot distribution, Kafka consumer lag — each a network call in production. A tool that runs for thirty silent seconds teaches the host to time out and retry. Progress notifications teach it to wait.

The mechanics are one line per stage:

await ctx.report_progress((i + 1) / len(stages), 1.0, stage_name)

On the wire that is notifications/progress with {progressToken, progress, total, message}. The client asked for it by passing progress_callback to call_tool; the SDK attaches the progressToken to the request's _meta automatically. The test collects every event and asserts stage order (database-pool, redis-slots, kafka-lag), monotonic progress, and a final value of exactly 1.0.

The diagnostic providers themselves are mocks with fixed seeds, and they are supposed to look alarming: the pool sits above 90% with waiting queries, three Redis hash slots have no serving node, and one Kafka partition lags past 50,000 messages. The verdict comes back DEGRADED. A triage system whose diagnostics always read healthy is a decoration.

8.7 Cryptographic human-in-the-loop

Here is the threat model. The agent proposes a rollback. A human must approve it. If approval is a boolean the agent can set — a tool argument, a prompt injection, a "the user said yes" — then the human is decoration. The approval must be something the agent cannot produce. That is what the HMAC buys.

The flow takes two calls. Call one carries no token. The server mints a challenge (chal_ + 8 random bytes), stores it with an expiry, and returns it pending. Nothing mutates. The pending response includes everything the approver needs: challenge id, action, target, expiry epoch, and the exact CLI invocation to mint the token.

Call two carries the token. The human minted it out-of-band with the shared secret — the approve subcommand in host.py, a command the agent never runs and whose secret it never sees. The token layout is v1.<challenge_id>.<expiry_epoch>.<hex_signature>, self-describing so the server can parse it before trusting it. Verification is four checks in order:

  1. signature, via hmac.compare_digest (constant time, no oracle);
  2. expiry;
  3. store lookup with single-use enforcement (consume before executing, so a crash cannot double-apply);
  4. action/target binding (a token minted for a scale cannot authorize a rollback).
def verify_approval_token(secret, token, action, target):
    _, challenge_id, expiry, sig = parse_approval_token(token)
    if time.time() >= expiry:
        raise ExpiredChallengeError("approval token expired")
    expected = _signature(secret, challenge_id, action, target, expiry)
    if not hmac.compare_digest(expected, sig):
        raise ApprovalError("approval token signature mismatch")
    return challenge_id, expiry

Challenges live in Redis in production — SET with EX gives expiry enforcement for free, and deleting on consume makes replayed tokens fail the store lookup even while their signature is still valid. Tests use the in-memory store: same interface, no daemon. The approval secret is required at startup; the server refuses to serve mutations without it. Fail fast at boot, not mid-incident.

8.8 The host: the triage loop

The host is where the agency lives, and it is deliberately boring. Six steps, each printing one JSON trace line:

  1. Detect. Open a listen() subscription on the service's log URI, read the current tail, count ERROR lines.
  2. Summarize. Call summarize_incident_logs; the mock sampler returns the diagnostic report; print it.
  3. Diagnose. Call run_distributed_diagnostic with a progress callback that renders a live checklist.
  4. Propose. Read the deployment manifests, call rollback_deployment with no token, get the pending challenge. Print the challenge id and the exact approver command.
  5. Wait. Block on stdin for the out-of-band token. The agent cannot mint it, cannot guess it, cannot proceed without it. Empty input aborts.
  6. Execute. Call rollback_deployment again with the token. The server verifies and mutates, or rejects with a reason.

The sampling callback is the seam to study. It receives the full 5,000-line prompt, extracts the log section, counts exception types with a regex, and returns the four-section report. Replace that function body with your model call and the whole system runs against a real LLM — nothing else changes.

8.9 Running it

The test suite needs no Docker, no network, and no API keys:

cd code/capstone-2
PYTHONPATH=$PWD ../../.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/ -q

For the full loop, serve the server and run the host. Terminal one:

SRE_APPROVAL_SECRET='dev-secret' SRE_ROTATION_INTERVAL_S=15 \
PYTHONPATH=$PWD ../../.venv/bin/python -m sre_mcp.server --transport streamable-http

Terminal two runs the triage loop against http://localhost:8000/mcp with PYTHONPATH=$PWD ../../.venv/bin/python -m sre_mcp.host triage. When it proposes the rollback, mint the token in terminal three as the on-call engineer with python -m sre_mcp.host approve --secret dev-secret --challenge-id … --action rollback_deployment --target payments-api --expires-at … (the pending challenge prints the exact values) and paste it at the prompt. The --transport stdio form serves one client over stdin/stdout for host embeddings.

Run this on a Docker-equipped machine — not in a sandbox. docker compose up --build starts the full topology: the SRE server on port 8000, Redis for challenge storage, and the mock observability API on port 9000. Set SRE_APPROVAL_SECRET to a real secret first.

8.10 Full source

The book stands alone: every file below is embedded in full, byte-identical to code/capstone-2/. The directory tree:

code/capstone-2/
├── pyproject.toml
├── docker-compose.yml
├── Dockerfile
├── README.md
├── sre_mcp/
│   ├── __init__.py

│   ├── synthetic.py       seeded synthetic stack-trace generator
│   ├── observability.py   mock logs / K8s / metrics / diagnostic providers
│   ├── approvals.py       HMAC tokens + ApprovalStore (memory + Redis)
│   ├── server.py          MCPServer factory: resources, tools, rotation
│   └── host.py            triage-loop client + out-of-band approver CLI
├── mock_observability/

└── tests/
    ├── __init__.py

pyproject.toml:

[project]
name = "sre-mcp-capstone"
version = "1.0.0"
description = "Capstone 2: Autonomous SRE & Incident Triage MCP platform (mcp 2.x)"
requires-python = ">=3.12"
dependencies = [
    "mcp>=2.0",
    "fastapi",

[tool.setuptools.packages.find]

sre_mcp/config.py — every knob comes from the environment so the same image runs in tests, compose, and production:

"""Runtime configuration for the SRE MCP server.

Every knob comes from the environment so the same image runs in tests
(defaults), in docker-compose, and in production. No secrets are hardcoded:
the approval HMAC secret must be injected (tests pass their own).
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import os

from pydantic import BaseModel, Field


class Settings(BaseModel):
    """Environment-driven settings. Instantiate once, pass down explicitly."""

    approval_secret: str = Field(
        default="",
        description="Shared HMAC secret used to mint/verify out-of-band approval tokens. "
        "Empty in tests (the harness injects its own); REQUIRED in production.",
    )
    approval_ttl_seconds: int = Field(
        default=600,
        description="How long a pending approval challenge stays valid.",
    )
    redis_url: str | None = Field(
        default=None,
        description="When set, challenges persist in Redis; otherwise in-memory.",
    )
    observability_base_url: str | None = Field(
        default=None,
        description="When set, reads logs/metrics from the mock observability HTTP "
        "service instead of the in-process mocks.",
    )
    rotation_interval_seconds: float = Field(
        default=30.0,
        description="Background log/metric rotation cadence. Tests shrink this.",
    )
    server_host: str = "0.0.0.0"
    server_port: int = 8000


def load_settings() -> Settings:
    """Build Settings from the environment. Keeps os.environ reads in one place."""
    return Settings(
        approval_secret=os.environ.get("SRE_APPROVAL_SECRET", ""),
        approval_ttl_seconds=int(os.environ.get("SRE_APPROVAL_TTL_S", "600")),
        redis_url=os.environ.get("SRE_REDIS_URL"),
        observability_base_url=os.environ.get("SRE_OBSERVABILITY_URL"),
        rotation_interval_seconds=float(os.environ.get("SRE_ROTATION_INTERVAL_S", "30.0")),
        server_host=os.environ.get("SRE_HOST", "0.0.0.0"),
        server_port=int(os.environ.get("SRE_PORT", "8000")),
    )

sre_mcp/synthetic.py — deterministic incident data. Same seed, same bytes, every run; no external data, no network:

"""Deterministic synthetic observability data.

Production incident logs are the one input this capstone refuses to fake with
hand-written fixtures: `generate_stack_traces` builds 5,000 lines of realistic
stack-trace noise from a seeded PRNG. Same seed → same bytes, every run, so
the sampling test can assert on exact line counts and the mock host summary is
reproducible. No external data, no network.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import random
from datetime import datetime, timedelta, timezone

# A small zoo of failure shapes. The generator weaves them into multi-line
# Python tracebacks so the summarizer has real structure to chew on.
_EXCEPTION_TEMPLATES = [
    (
        "TimeoutError",
        "Timed out after {ms}ms waiting for upstream {svc}",
        [
            '  File "/app/{svc}/client.py", line {ln}, in fetch',
            "    resp = pool.request(path, timeout={ms})",
            '  File "/app/{svc}/pool.py", line {ln2}, in request',
            "    raise TimeoutError(f\"Timed out after {ms}ms waiting for upstream {svc}\")",
        ],
    ),
    (
        "ConnectionRefusedError",
        "[Errno 111] Connection refused -> {svc}:{port}",
        [
            '  File "/app/{svc}/client.py", line {ln}, in connect',
            "    sock.connect((host, {port}))",
            "ConnectionRefusedError: [Errno 111] Connection refused",
        ],
    ),
    (
        "psycopg2.OperationalError",
        'FATAL: remaining connection slots are reserved for superuser (pool exhausted on "{db}")',
        [
            '  File "/app/{svc}/db.py", line {ln}, in get_conn',
            "    return pool.acquire()",
            '  File "/app/vendor/pool.py", line {ln2}, in acquire',
            'psycopg2.OperationalError: FATAL: remaining connection slots are reserved',
        ],
    ),
    (
        "kafka.errors.NotLeaderForPartitionError",
        "Broker {broker} is not leader for partition {part}",
        [
            '  File "/app/{svc}/consumer.py", line {ln}, in poll',
            "    batch = consumer.poll(timeout_ms={ms})",
            "kafka.errors.NotLeaderForPartitionError: Broker {broker} is not leader",
        ],
    ),
    (
        "redis.exceptions.ResponseError",
        "CLUSTERDOWN Hash slot not served (slot {slot})",
        [
            '  File "/app/{svc}/cache.py", line {ln}, in get',
            "    return client.get(key)",
            "redis.exceptions.ResponseError: CLUSTERDOWN Hash slot not served",
        ],
    ),
    (
        "ValueError",
        "could not convert string to float: '{badval}' (schema drift in {svc} payload)",
        [
            '  File "/app/{svc}/serializers.py", line {ln}, in parse',
            "    return float(raw)",
            "ValueError: could not convert string to float",
        ],
    ),
]

_SERVICES = ["payments-api", "orders-api", "inventory-svc", "auth-gateway"]
_HOSTS = ["ip-10-0-4-21", "ip-10-0-4-22", "ip-10-0-5-11", "ip-10-0-6-7"]
_LEVELS = ["ERROR", "ERROR", "ERROR", "WARN", "INFO"]  # errors dominate: it is an incident


def _one_trace(rng: random.Random, service: str, ts: datetime) -> list[str]:
    """Render one multi-line traceback. Deterministic given `rng`."""
    exc, msg_tpl, frame_tpl = rng.choice(_EXCEPTION_TEMPLATES)
    host = rng.choice(_HOSTS)
    ctx = {
        "svc": service,
        "ms": rng.choice([2000, 5000, 10000, 30000]),
        "ln": rng.randint(40, 400),
        "ln2": rng.randint(10, 120),
        "port": rng.choice([5432, 6379, 9092, 8080]),
        "broker": rng.randint(1, 3),
        "part": rng.randint(0, 23),
        "slot": rng.randint(0, 16383),
        "db": rng.choice(["orders", "payments", "inventory"]),
        "badval": rng.choice(["NaN", "None", "inf", ""]),
    }
    stamp = ts.strftime("%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S.%f")[:-3] + "Z"
    lines = [f"{stamp} {rng.choice(_LEVELS)} [{host}] {service} - Traceback (most recent call last):"]
    lines += [f.format(**ctx) for f in frame_tpl]
    lines.append(f"{exc}: {msg_tpl.format(**ctx)}")
    # Occasionally a chained cause, like real cascading failures.
    if rng.random() < 0.15:
        lines.append("During handling of the above exception, another exception occurred:")
        lines.append(f"{stamp} RuntimeError: retry budget exhausted for {service} (3/3 attempts)")
    return lines


def generate_stack_traces(seed: int, lines: int, service: str = "payments-api") -> list[str]:
    """Generate exactly `lines` synthetic log lines. Seeded → deterministic.

    Timestamps walk backwards from "now" so the tail reads like a live log.
    """
    rng = random.Random(seed)
    out: list[str] = []
    ts = datetime.now(timezone.utc)
    while len(out) < lines:
        out.extend(_one_trace(rng, service, ts))
        ts -= timedelta(milliseconds=rng.randint(50, 900))
    return out[:lines]


def seed_for(service: str) -> int:
    """Stable seed per service name so every service has its own fixed incident."""
    return int.from_bytes(service.encode()[:8].ljust(8, b"\0"), "big") % (2**31)

sre_mcp/observability.py — the whole downstream world, mocked. The mocks are stateful on purpose: MockKubernetes.mutations is the list the HITL tests assert against, and rotate() is what the background task calls:

"""Mocked observability plane for the SRE capstone.

Everything downstream of the MCP server is a mock: log storage, Kubernetes
deployments, and the three diagnostic providers (database pool, Redis slots,
Kafka lag). Mocks keep the whole system runnable with zero Docker — the
docker-compose file swaps in an HTTP observability stub for the full
multi-container topology (marked run-on-Mac).

The mocks are deliberately stateful: `rotate()` mutates logs and metrics the
way a live system would, and `MockKubernetes.rollback()` is the single
mutation point the HITL gate protects. Tests assert against that state.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import random
import time
from collections import deque
from typing import Any

import httpx
from pydantic import BaseModel, Field

from .synthetic import generate_stack_traces, seed_for


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Domain models
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
class Deployment(BaseModel):
    name: str
    cluster: str
    revision: str
    replicas: int
    status: str = "healthy"
    image: str = ""


class MetricSnapshot(BaseModel):
    cluster: str
    captured_at: float
    cpu_percent: float
    memory_percent: float
    p99_latency_ms: float
    error_rate: float


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Log store
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
class LogStore:
    """Append-only per-service log buffers with tail reads."""

    def __init__(self, capacity: int = 20_000) -> None:
        self._logs: dict[str, deque[str]] = {}
        self._capacity = capacity

    def seed_service(self, service: str, lines: int = 5_000) -> None:
        self._logs[service] = deque(
            generate_stack_traces(seed_for(service), lines, service),
            maxlen=self._capacity,
        )

    def append(self, service: str, lines: list[str]) -> None:
        buf = self._logs.setdefault(service, deque(maxlen=self._capacity))
        buf.extend(lines)

    def tail(self, service: str, lines: int = 200) -> list[str]:
        return list(self._logs.get(service, deque()))[-lines:]

    def line_count(self, service: str) -> int:
        return len(self._logs.get(service, ()))

    def services(self) -> list[str]:
        return sorted(self._logs)


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Mock Kubernetes — the mutation surface the HITL gate protects
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
class MockKubernetes:
    def __init__(self) -> None:
        self.deployments: dict[str, Deployment] = {
            "payments-api": Deployment(
                name="payments-api",
                cluster="prod-us-east",
                revision="r184",
                replicas=12,
                image="registry.internal/payments-api:r184",
            ),
            "orders-api": Deployment(
                name="orders-api",
                cluster="prod-us-east",
                revision="r211",
                replicas=8,
                image="registry.internal/orders-api:r211",
            ),
        }
        # Every executed mutation lands here. Tests assert on this list:
        # empty means the HITL gate held.
        self.mutations: list[dict[str, Any]] = []

    def rollback(self, name: str, target_revision: str) -> Deployment:
        dep = self.deployments[name]  # KeyError → unknown deployment: fail loudly
        previous = dep.revision
        dep.revision = target_revision
        dep.image = f"registry.internal/{name}:{target_revision}"
        dep.status = "rolling-back"
        self.mutations.append(
            {
                "action": "rollback",
                "deployment": name,
                "from": previous,
                "to": target_revision,
                "at": time.time(),
            }
        )
        return dep

    def scale(self, name: str, replicas: int) -> Deployment:
        dep = self.deployments[name]
        previous = dep.replicas
        dep.replicas = replicas
        self.mutations.append(
            {"action": "scale", "deployment": name, "from": previous, "to": replicas, "at": time.time()}
        )
        return dep


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Mock observability facade
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
class MockObservability:
    """One object behind all three resource templates and the diagnostics."""

    def __init__(self) -> None:
        self.logs = LogStore()
        for svc in ("payments-api", "orders-api", "inventory-svc"):
            self.logs.seed_service(svc)
        self.k8s = MockKubernetes()
        self._metrics: dict[str, MetricSnapshot] = {}
        self._rotation = 0
        for cluster in ("prod-us-east", "prod-eu-west"):
            self._metrics[cluster] = self._fresh_metrics(cluster)

    # -- resources ---------------------------------------------------------
    def recent_manifests(self, cluster: str) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
        return [
            d.model_dump()
            for d in self.k8s.deployments.values()
            if d.cluster == cluster
        ]

    def recent_logs(self, service: str, lines: int = 200) -> list[str]:
        return self.logs.tail(service, lines)

    def metrics_snapshot(self, cluster: str) -> dict[str, Any]:
        return self._metrics[cluster].model_dump()

    # -- rotation: simulates a live system between reads --------------------
    def rotate(self) -> dict[str, list[str]]:
        """Append fresh synthetic lines, jitter metrics. Returns URIs to notify."""
        self._rotation += 1
        rng = random.Random(10_000 + self._rotation)
        touched: list[str] = []
        for svc in self.logs.services():
            # A burst of new errors, like the incident is still unfolding.
            new_lines = generate_stack_traces(
                seed=90_000 + self._rotation * 7 + hash(svc) % 1000,
                lines=rng.randint(25, 60),
                service=svc,
            )
            self.logs.append(svc, new_lines)
            touched.append(f"logs://service/{svc}/recent")
        for cluster in self._metrics:
            self._metrics[cluster] = self._fresh_metrics(cluster)
            touched.append(f"cluster://{cluster}/metrics")
        return {"updated_uris": touched, "rotation": self._rotation}

    def _fresh_metrics(self, cluster: str) -> MetricSnapshot:
        rng = random.Random(hash(cluster) % (2**31) + self._rotation)
        return MetricSnapshot(
            cluster=cluster,
            captured_at=time.time(),
            cpu_percent=round(rng.uniform(55, 92), 1),
            memory_percent=round(rng.uniform(60, 88), 1),
            p99_latency_ms=round(rng.uniform(180, 2400), 1),
            error_rate=round(rng.uniform(0.02, 0.31), 3),
        )

    # -- distributed diagnostics: three mocked providers --------------------
    def check_database_pool(self) -> dict[str, Any]:
        rng = random.Random(4242)
        used = rng.randint(88, 99)
        return {
            "provider": "database-pool",
            "pool_used_percent": used,
            "waiting_queries": rng.randint(12, 64),
            "status": "degraded" if used > 90 else "ok",
            "detail": "acquire() latency p99 2.1s; pool near exhaustion on 'payments' DB",
        }

    def check_redis_slots(self) -> dict[str, Any]:
        rng = random.Random(777)
        uncovered = sorted(rng.sample(range(16384), 3))
        return {
            "provider": "redis-slots",
            "uncovered_slots": uncovered,
            "migrating_slots": rng.randint(0, 128),
            "status": "degraded" if uncovered else "ok",
            "detail": f"CLUSTERDOWN risk: slots {uncovered} have no serving node",
        }

    def check_kafka_lag(self) -> dict[str, Any]:
        rng = random.Random(31337)
        lag = {f"payments-events-{p}": rng.randint(4_000, 120_000) for p in range(6)}
        worst = max(lag.values())
        return {
            "provider": "kafka-lag",
            "consumer_group": "sre-triage",
            "partition_lag": lag,
            "status": "degraded" if worst > 50_000 else "ok",
            "detail": f"worst lag {worst} msgs; consumer group rebalancing after broker flap",
        }


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# HTTP observability client (docker-compose topology; run-on-Mac)
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
class HttpObservability:
    """Same shape as MockObservability, backed by the mock-observability service.

    Only used when SRE_OBSERVABILITY_URL is set (docker-compose). Kept
    deliberately thin: the mock service returns JSON shaped like the models
    above.
    """

    def __init__(self, base_url: str) -> None:
        self._client = httpx.Client(base_url=base_url, timeout=10.0)

    def recent_logs(self, service: str, lines: int = 200) -> list[str]:
        r = self._client.get(f"/logs/{service}", params={"lines": lines})
        r.raise_for_status()
        return r.json()["lines"]

    def recent_manifests(self, cluster: str) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
        r = self._client.get(f"/clusters/{cluster}/deployments")
        r.raise_for_status()
        return r.json()["deployments"]

    def metrics_snapshot(self, cluster: str) -> dict[str, Any]:
        r = self._client.get(f"/clusters/{cluster}/metrics")
        r.raise_for_status()
        return r.json()

sre_mcp/approvals.py — the cryptographic core. Read the module docstring first; it states the whole governance model in one paragraph:

"""Cryptographic human-in-the-loop approvals.

The governance model: a mutating tool NEVER executes on the agent's word
alone. The first call creates a *challenge* and returns it pending. A human
(on-call engineer) reviews the challenge out-of-band and mints an HMAC-SHA256
token over (challenge_id, action, target, expiry) with a secret the MCP server
never reveals to the agent. The second call carries the token; the server
verifies signature + expiry + single-use before touching infrastructure.

Why HMAC instead of a shared boolean flag: a flag can be set by the agent
itself ("the user said yes" in a prompt). An HMAC token can only be produced
by whoever holds the secret — which lives in the on-call's vault, not in the
agent's context. The token is self-describing (challenge id + expiry ride
inside it), so verification needs no extra round trip.

Challenges persist in Redis in production (survive restarts, shared across
server replicas); tests use the in-memory store.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import hashlib
import hmac
import json
import secrets
import time
from typing import Protocol

from pydantic import BaseModel, Field


class ApprovalError(Exception):
    """Raised when a token fails verification. Never leaks the secret."""


class ExpiredChallengeError(ApprovalError):
    pass


class ApprovalChallenge(BaseModel):
    challenge_id: str
    action: str  # e.g. "rollback_deployment"
    target: str  # e.g. "payments-api"
    detail: dict = Field(default_factory=dict)
    created_at: float
    expires_at: float
    consumed: bool = False

    @property
    def expired(self) -> bool:
        return time.time() >= self.expires_at


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Token minting / verification (shared by server + out-of-band approver CLI)
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
TOKEN_VERSION = "v1"


def _signature(secret: str, challenge_id: str, action: str, target: str, expires_at: int) -> str:
    """HMAC-SHA256 over the canonical payload. Secret never leaves the holder."""
    payload = f"{TOKEN_VERSION}:{challenge_id}:{action}:{target}:{expires_at}".encode()
    return hmac.new(secret.encode(), payload, hashlib.sha256).hexdigest()


def mint_approval_token(
    secret: str,
    challenge_id: str,
    action: str,
    target: str,
    expires_at: float,
) -> str:
    """Minted OUT-OF-BAND by the human approver (approve CLI), never by the agent.

    Token layout: `v1.<challenge_id>.<expiry_epoch>.<hex_signature>` — the
    server can parse challenge_id/expiry without a store lookup, then verify
    the signature before trusting either field.
    """
    expiry = int(expires_at)
    sig = _signature(secret, challenge_id, action, target, expiry)
    return f"{TOKEN_VERSION}.{challenge_id}.{expiry}.{sig}"


def parse_approval_token(token: str) -> tuple[str, str, int, str]:
    """Split a token into (version, challenge_id, expiry_epoch, signature)."""
    parts = token.split(".")
    if len(parts) != 4 or parts[0] != TOKEN_VERSION:
        raise ApprovalError("malformed approval token")
    _, challenge_id, expiry_s, sig = parts
    try:
        return TOKEN_VERSION, challenge_id, int(expiry_s), sig
    except ValueError:
        raise ApprovalError("malformed approval token") from None


def verify_approval_token(
    secret: str, token: str, action: str, target: str
) -> tuple[str, int]:
    """Verify signature and expiry. Returns (challenge_id, expiry_epoch).

    Raises ApprovalError on bad signature, ExpiredChallengeError on stale
    tokens. Uses compare_digest so verification time doesn't leak the key.
    """
    _, challenge_id, expiry, sig = parse_approval_token(token)
    if time.time() >= expiry:
        raise ExpiredChallengeError("approval token expired")
    expected = _signature(secret, challenge_id, action, target, expiry)
    if not hmac.compare_digest(expected, sig):
        raise ApprovalError("approval token signature mismatch")
    return challenge_id, expiry


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Challenge store: in-memory for tests, Redis for production
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
class ApprovalStore(Protocol):
    async def create(self, challenge: ApprovalChallenge) -> None: ...
    async def get(self, challenge_id: str) -> ApprovalChallenge | None: ...
    async def consume(self, challenge_id: str) -> None: ...


class InMemoryApprovalStore:
    """Test/dev store. Single process, no persistence — fine for the harness."""

    def __init__(self) -> None:
        self._challenges: dict[str, ApprovalChallenge] = {}

    async def create(self, challenge: ApprovalChallenge) -> None:
        self._challenges[challenge.challenge_id] = challenge

    async def get(self, challenge_id: str) -> ApprovalChallenge | None:
        return self._challenges.get(challenge_id)

    async def consume(self, challenge_id: str) -> None:
        if (c := self._challenges.get(challenge_id)) is not None:
            c.consumed = True


def new_challenge(action: str, target: str, detail: dict, ttl_seconds: int) -> ApprovalChallenge:
    now = time.time()
    return ApprovalChallenge(
        challenge_id=f"chal_{secrets.token_hex(8)}",
        action=action,
        target=target,
        detail=detail,
        created_at=now,
        expires_at=now + ttl_seconds,
    )


class RedisApprovalStore:
    """Production sketch: challenges in Redis with native TTL.

    > Run the Redis path on a Docker-equipped machine — not in a sandbox.
    Only constructed when SRE_REDIS_URL is set, so unit tests never touch it.
    """

    def __init__(self, redis_url: str) -> None:
        import redis.asyncio as redis  # local import: optional dependency at runtime

        self._redis = redis.from_url(redis_url, decode_responses=True)

    def _key(self, challenge_id: str) -> str:
        return f"sre:approval:{challenge_id}"

    async def create(self, challenge: ApprovalChallenge) -> None:
        ttl = max(1, int(challenge.expires_at - time.time()))
        # SET with EX gives us expiry enforcement for free — even if the
        # server forgets to check, Redis deletes the challenge.
        await self._redis.set(self._key(challenge.challenge_id), challenge.model_dump_json(), ex=ttl)

    async def get(self, challenge_id: str) -> ApprovalChallenge | None:
        raw = await self._redis.get(self._key(challenge_id))
        return ApprovalChallenge.model_validate(json.loads(raw)) if raw else None

    async def consume(self, challenge_id: str) -> None:
        # Single-use: delete on consume. A replayed token then fails the
        # store lookup even if its signature is still valid.
        await self._redis.delete(self._key(challenge_id))

    async def close(self) -> None:
        await self._redis.aclose()

sre_mcp/server.py — the MCPServer factory. Everything the chapter teaches lives here: resource templates, sampling, progress, the HITL gate, and the rotation background task:

"""The SRE MCP server (MCPServer 2.x, Streamable HTTP).

Exposes the incident-triage surface:

Resources (dynamic templates):
  k8s://clusters/{cluster}/deployments   recent manifests
  logs://service/{name}/recent           tailing error logs
  cluster://{cluster}/metrics             live metrics snapshot

Tools:
  summarize_incident_logs   sampling/nested-LLM log summarization
  run_distributed_diagnostic  long-running checks with progress streaming
  rollback_deployment / scale_worker_pool  cryptographic HITL remediation

A lifespan background task rotates logs/metrics and publishes
`ResourceUpdated` events to `subscriptions/listen` streams — the 2.x
successor to `resources/subscribe` (see the protocol-version note in the
chapter). On the legacy 2025-era wire the same notification travels as
`notifications/resources/updated` via `ctx.session.send_resource_updated()`.

1.x → 2.x rename note: this file's `MCPServer` is what 1.x called `FastMCP`.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import asyncio
import json
import time
from collections.abc import AsyncIterator
from contextlib import asynccontextmanager
from typing import Any

from mcp.server.mcpserver import Context, MCPServer
from mcp.shared.subscriptions import ResourceUpdated
from mcp.types import SamplingMessage, TextContent

from .approvals import (
    ApprovalChallenge,
    ApprovalError,
    ExpiredChallengeError,
    InMemoryApprovalStore,
    RedisApprovalStore,
    new_challenge,
    verify_approval_token,
)
from .config import Settings, load_settings
from .observability import HttpObservability, MockObservability
from .synthetic import generate_stack_traces, seed_for

SERVER_NAME = "sre-triage-mcp"
SERVER_VERSION = "1.0.0"

# Number of raw log lines the sampling tool pulls before asking the host
# to summarize. Large enough that no host would paste it into chat by hand.
INCIDENT_LOG_LINES = 5_000


def create_server(
    settings: Settings | None = None,
    observability: MockObservability | HttpObservability | None = None,
    approval_store: InMemoryApprovalStore | RedisApprovalStore | None = None,
) -> MCPServer:
    """Factory: builds a fully-wired server with injectable dependencies.

    Tests inject mocks + a fast rotation interval. Production calls
    `create_server()` with no args and reads everything from the environment.
    """
    settings = settings or load_settings()
    obs = observability or (
        HttpObservability(settings.observability_base_url)
        if settings.observability_base_url
        else MockObservability()
    )
    store = approval_store or (
        RedisApprovalStore(settings.redis_url) if settings.redis_url else InMemoryApprovalStore()
    )
    # The approval secret is REQUIRED for any mutation path. Fail fast at
    # startup rather than mid-incident.
    secret = settings.approval_secret

    @asynccontextmanager
    async def lifespan(server: MCPServer) -> AsyncIterator[dict[str, Any]]:
        """Start the rotation loop; it lives as long as the server does."""
        stop = asyncio.Event()
        task = asyncio.create_task(
            _rotation_loop(server, obs, stop, settings.rotation_interval_seconds),
            name="sre-rotation",
        )
        try:
            yield {"observability": obs, "approvals": store, "settings": settings}
        finally:
            stop.set()
            await task
            if isinstance(store, RedisApprovalStore):
                await store.close()

    server = MCPServer(SERVER_NAME, version=SERVER_VERSION, lifespan=lifespan)

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Resources
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    @server.resource("k8s://clusters/{cluster}/deployments")
    def cluster_deployments(cluster: str) -> str:
        """Recent deployment manifests for a cluster."""
        manifests = obs.recent_manifests(cluster)
        return json.dumps({"cluster": cluster, "deployments": manifests}, indent=2)

    @server.resource("logs://service/{name}/recent")
    def service_logs(name: str) -> str:
        """Tail of the error log for a service — the triage starting point."""
        lines = obs.recent_logs(name, lines=200)
        return "\n".join(lines)

    @server.resource("cluster://{cluster}/metrics")
    def cluster_metrics(cluster: str) -> str:
        """Live metrics snapshot: CPU, memory, p99 latency, error rate."""
        return json.dumps(obs.metrics_snapshot(cluster), indent=2)

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Tools
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    @server.tool()
    async def summarize_incident_logs(ctx: Context, service: str) -> dict[str, Any]:
        """Pull 5,000 raw log lines and ask the HOST to summarize them.

        Sampling pattern: the server never holds an LLM API key. It ships the
        evidence to the host via `sampling/createMessage`; the host's model
        does the reasoning and returns a diagnostic report. The server stays
        a dumb, auditable pipe — reasoning lives one level up, where the
        human can see it.
        """
        raw = generate_stack_traces(seed_for(service), INCIDENT_LOG_LINES, service)
        prompt = (
            f"You are an SRE diagnostician. Below are {len(raw)} raw log lines "
            f"from service '{service}' during an active incident.\n"
            "Return a diagnostic report with exactly these sections:\n"
            "1. TOP EXCEPTIONS (ranked, with counts)\n"
            "2. LIKELY ROOT CAUSE (one paragraph)\n"
            "3. BLAST RADIUS (which dependencies are implicated)\n"
            "4. SUGGESTED NEXT CHECK (one concrete probe)\n\n"
            "--- BEGIN LOGS ---\n" + "\n".join(raw) + "\n--- END LOGS ---"
        )
        # Server-initiated LLM call. The host answers through its
        # sampling_callback; without one, this raises.
        result = await ctx.session.create_message(
            messages=[SamplingMessage(role="user", content=TextContent(type="text", text=prompt))],
            max_tokens=1000,
            system_prompt="You are a terse SRE assistant. No preamble, just the report.",
        )
        report = result.content.text if hasattr(result.content, "text") else str(result.content)
        return {
            "service": service,
            "lines_analyzed": len(raw),
            "diagnostic_report": report,
        }

    @server.tool()
    async def simulate_incident_burst(ctx: Context, service: str) -> dict[str, Any]:
        """Game-day helper: inject a burst of synthetic errors, notify subscribers.

        Appends fresh error lines to the service log, then pushes the update
        through BOTH notification paths so hosts on either wire era see it:
          * `ctx.notify_resource_updated` → typed ResourceUpdated on
            `subscriptions/listen` streams (2.x modern path);
          * `ctx.session.send_resource_updated` → `notifications/resources/updated`
            for hosts that subscribed via the legacy `resources/subscribe`.
        """
        uri = f"logs://service/{service}/recent"
        burst = generate_stack_traces(seed_for(service + ":burst"), 120, service)
        if isinstance(obs, MockObservability):
            obs.logs.append(service, burst)
        await ctx.notify_resource_updated(uri)
        await ctx.session.send_resource_updated(uri)
        return {"service": service, "uri": uri, "lines_injected": len(burst)}

    @server.tool()
    async def run_distributed_diagnostic(ctx: Context) -> dict[str, Any]:
        """Check DB pools, Redis slots, and Kafka lag with progress streaming.

        Long-running by design: each provider probe is a network call in
        production. Progress notifications let the host render a live
        checklist instead of staring at a spinner.
        """
        # HttpObservability (compose) has no probe endpoints: probes stay simulated.
        probes = obs if isinstance(obs, MockObservability) else MockObservability()
        stages = [
            ("database-pool", probes.check_database_pool),
            ("redis-slots", probes.check_redis_slots),
            ("kafka-lag", probes.check_kafka_lag),
        ]
        findings: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
        for i, (stage_name, probe) in enumerate(stages):
            # progress, total, message → notifications/progress on the wire.
            await ctx.report_progress((i + 1) / len(stages), 1.0, stage_name)
            await asyncio.sleep(0)  # yield: probes are I/O-bound in prod
            findings.append(probe())
        degraded = [f["provider"] for f in findings if f["status"] == "degraded"]
        return {
            "findings": findings,
            "degraded": degraded,
            "verdict": "DEGRADED — investigate providers above" if degraded else "HEALTHY",
        }

    async def _guarded_mutation(
        ctx: Context,
        action: str,
        target: str,
        detail: dict[str, Any],
        approval_token: str | None,
        execute: Any,
    ) -> dict[str, Any]:
        """The HITL gate both mutating tools share. Two calls, one gate.

        Call 1 (no token) → returns a pending challenge, mutates NOTHING.
        Call 2 (HMAC token minted out-of-band by a human) → verifies
        signature, expiry, and single-use, then executes exactly once.
        """
        _ = ctx  # ctx reserved: future per-request audit identity lands here
        if approval_token is None:
            challenge = new_challenge(action, target, detail, settings.approval_ttl_seconds)
            await store.create(challenge)
            return {
                "status": "pending_approval",
                "challenge_id": challenge.challenge_id,
                "action": action,
                "target": target,
                "expires_at": challenge.expires_at,
                "expires_in_seconds": settings.approval_ttl_seconds,
                "instructions": (
                    "A human approver must mint an approval token OUT-OF-BAND: "
                    "python -m sre_mcp.host approve --secret $SRE_APPROVAL_SECRET "
                    "--challenge-id {cid} --action {action} "
                    "--target {target} --expires-at {exp}".format(
                        cid=challenge.challenge_id, action=action, target=target,
                        exp=int(challenge.expires_at),
                    )
                ),
            }
        # --- token path: verify before touching anything -----------------
        try:
            challenge_id, _expiry = verify_approval_token(secret, approval_token, action, target)
        except ExpiredChallengeError:
            return {"status": "rejected", "reason": "challenge_expired",
                    "detail": "The approval window lapsed. Propose the action again."}
        except ApprovalError as e:
            return {"status": "rejected", "reason": "invalid_token", "detail": str(e)}

        challenge: ApprovalChallenge | None = await store.get(challenge_id)
        if challenge is None or challenge.consumed:
            return {"status": "rejected", "reason": "unknown_or_consumed_challenge",
                    "detail": "Challenge not found or already used (replay rejected)."}
        if challenge.expired:
            return {"status": "rejected", "reason": "challenge_expired",
                    "detail": "Challenge expired server-side. Propose the action again."}
        if challenge.action != action or challenge.target != target:
            return {"status": "rejected", "reason": "challenge_mismatch",
                    "detail": "Token was minted for a different action/target."}

        await store.consume(challenge_id)  # single-use: consume BEFORE executing
        result = execute()
        return {"status": "executed", "action": action, "target": target,
                "challenge_id": challenge_id, "result": result}

    @server.tool()
    async def rollback_deployment(
        ctx: Context,
        deployment: str,
        target_revision: str,
        approval_token: str | None = None,
    ) -> dict[str, Any]:
        """Roll back a deployment — ONLY with a valid out-of-band approval token.

        Without `approval_token` this returns a pending challenge and changes
        nothing. With a token, the HMAC signature, expiry, and single-use are
        verified before the rollback executes.
        """
        return await _guarded_mutation(
            ctx,
            action="rollback_deployment",
            target=deployment,
            detail={"target_revision": target_revision},
            approval_token=approval_token,
            execute=lambda: obs.k8s.rollback(deployment, target_revision).model_dump()
            if isinstance(obs, MockObservability)
            else {"deployment": deployment, "target_revision": target_revision, "mode": "http"},
        )

    @server.tool()
    async def scale_worker_pool(
        ctx: Context,
        pool: str,
        replicas: int,
        approval_token: str | None = None,
    ) -> dict[str, Any]:
        """Scale a worker pool — same HITL gate as rollback_deployment."""
        return await _guarded_mutation(
            ctx,
            action="scale_worker_pool",
            target=pool,
            detail={"replicas": replicas},
            approval_token=approval_token,
            execute=lambda: obs.k8s.scale(pool, replicas).model_dump()
            if isinstance(obs, MockObservability)
            else {"pool": pool, "replicas": replicas, "mode": "http"},
        )

    return server


async def _rotation_loop(
    server: MCPServer,
    obs: MockObservability | HttpObservability,
    stop: asyncio.Event,
    interval: float,
) -> None:
    """Background task: simulate a live system, push updates to subscribers.

    Each tick appends fresh synthetic log lines and jitters metrics, then
    publishes ResourceUpdated for every touched URI to `subscriptions/listen`
    streams. The publish goes through the server's subscription bus directly
    because there is no request context outside a tool call — this is the
    one place that reaches past `ctx`.
    """
    while not stop.is_set():
        try:  # wake at once on shutdown instead of sleeping out the interval
            await asyncio.wait_for(stop.wait(), timeout=interval)
            break
        except asyncio.TimeoutError:
            pass
        if isinstance(obs, MockObservability):
            rotated = obs.rotate()
            for uri in rotated["updated_uris"]:
                await server._subscriptions.publish(ResourceUpdated(uri=uri))


def main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> None:
    """Serve entrypoint: stdio (default, for tests/hosts) or Streamable HTTP."""
    import argparse

    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description="SRE triage MCP server")
    parser.add_argument(
        "--transport",
        choices=("stdio", "streamable-http"),
        default="stdio",
        help="stdio: serve one client over stdin/stdout. "
        "streamable-http: serve over HTTP (docker-compose / production).",
    )
    args = parser.parse_args(argv)

    settings = load_settings()
    server = create_server(settings)
    if args.transport == "stdio":
        server.run(transport="stdio")
    else:
        if not settings.approval_secret:
            raise SystemExit(
                "SRE_APPROVAL_SECRET must be set — refusing to serve mutations without it."
            )
        server.run(transport="streamable-http", host=settings.server_host, port=settings.server_port)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

sre_mcp/host.py — the triage loop and the approver CLI. The mock sampler is the seam where a production LLM plugs in:

"""Host client: the autonomous triage loop.

The host is where agency lives. It drives the whole incident workflow
against the SRE MCP server over Streamable HTTP:

  detect → summarize (sampling) → diagnose (progress) → propose → HITL → execute

Every step prints a structured JSON trace line so the run is auditable.

The sampling_callback below is a DETERMINISTIC MOCK — it parses the raw
lines the server sent and builds a fixed-shape report with no API keys.
In production this is exactly the seam where you plug in your LLM call;
the server never sees the difference.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import asyncio
import json
import re
import sys
import time
from collections import Counter
from typing import Any

from mcp import Client
from mcp.types import CreateMessageResult, TextContent

from .approvals import mint_approval_token

SERVER_URL = "http://localhost:8000/mcp"


def trace(event: str, **fields: Any) -> None:
    """Structured trace log: one JSON object per line, always flushed."""
    print(json.dumps({"ts": time.time(), "event": event, **fields}), flush=True)


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Deterministic mock sampler (no API keys)
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
async def mock_sampling_callback(context: Any, params: Any) -> CreateMessageResult:
    """Pretend to be the host LLM: count exceptions in the shipped log lines.

    The server sends ~5,000 lines inside the prompt. We extract the
    `ExceptionType: message` tail lines, rank them, and return a fixed-shape
    diagnostic report. Deterministic: same seed → same report.
    """
    prompt = params.messages[0].content.text
    log_section = prompt.split("--- BEGIN LOGS ---", 1)[1].rsplit("--- END LOGS ---", 1)[0]
    exc_pattern = re.compile(r"^([A-Za-z_][\w.]*Error|TimeoutError|ValueError):", re.M)
    counts = Counter(exc_pattern.findall(log_section))
    total = sum(counts.values())
    ranked = "\n".join(f"- {name}: {n} occurrences" for name, n in counts.most_common(5))
    top = counts.most_common(1)[0][0] if counts else "unknown"
    report = (
        "1. TOP EXCEPTIONS\n" + ranked
        + f"\n\n2. LIKELY ROOT CAUSE\nThe dominant failure is {top} "
        f"({counts[top]} of {total} exceptions). "
        "The pool-exhaustion and slot errors point at downstream saturation, not bad deploys."
        "\n\n3. BLAST RADIUS\npayments-api → orders DB pool, redis cluster, kafka consumer group sre-triage."
        "\n\n4. SUGGESTED NEXT CHECK\nRun run_distributed_diagnostic to confirm which provider is saturated."
    )
    trace("sampling_callback_invoked", lines_analyzed=len(log_section.strip("\n").splitlines()),
          exceptions_found=total)
    return CreateMessageResult(
        role="assistant",
        content=TextContent(type="text", text=report),
        model="mock-sre-sampler/1.0",
    )


async def on_progress(progress: float, total: float | None, message: str | None) -> None:
    bar = "#" * int((progress or 0) * 20)
    trace("diagnostic_progress", stage=message, percent=round((progress or 0) * 100),
          bar=bar)


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Triage loop
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Sampling needs the legacy connection; modern connections have no server-to-host request channel.
async def summarize_with_legacy_sampling(server_url: str, service: str) -> Any:
    """Run this compatibility example on a legacy protocol connection."""
    async with Client(server_url, mode="legacy",
                      sampling_callback=mock_sampling_callback) as sampling_client:
        return await sampling_client.call_tool("summarize_incident_logs",
                                               {"service": service})

async def triage(service: str, cluster: str, server_url: str = SERVER_URL) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """Run the full detect → summarize → diagnose → propose → approve → execute loop."""
    async with Client(server_url) as client:
        trace("host_connected", server=server_url)

        # 1. DETECT: subscribe to the log stream, then read the current tail.
        #    The listen() stream is the 2.x subscriptions/listen mechanism —
        #    it replaces the removed resources/subscribe on this wire.
        async with client.listen(
            resource_subscriptions=[f"logs://service/{service}/recent"]
        ) as sub:
            trace("subscribed", uri=f"logs://service/{service}/recent")
            tail = await client.read_resource(f"logs://service/{service}/recent")
            contents = tail.contents if hasattr(tail, "contents") else tail
            text = contents[0].text
            error_lines = sum(1 for ln in text.splitlines() if "ERROR" in ln)
            trace("detect", service=service, tail_lines=len(text.splitlines()),
                  error_lines=error_lines)

            # 2. SUMMARIZE using the separate legacy sampling connection.
            #    The modern client above handles subscriptions and the other calls.
            summary = await summarize_with_legacy_sampling(server_url, service)
            report = summary.structured_content["diagnostic_report"]
            trace("summarized", lines=summary.structured_content["lines_analyzed"],
                  report_chars=len(report))
            print("\n===== DIAGNOSTIC REPORT =====\n" + report + "\n=============================\n")

            # 3. DIAGNOSE with live progress: DB pool, Redis slots, Kafka lag.
            diag = await client.call_tool(
                "run_distributed_diagnostic", {}, progress_callback=on_progress)
            verdict = diag.structured_content["verdict"]
            degraded = diag.structured_content["degraded"]
            trace("diagnosed", verdict=verdict, degraded=degraded)

            # 4. PROPOSE: no token → the server returns a pending challenge
            #    and mutates nothing. This is the point of no return that
            #    ISN'T — the agent cannot cross it alone.
            manifests = await client.read_resource(f"k8s://clusters/{cluster}/deployments")
            mcontents = manifests.contents if hasattr(manifests, "contents") else manifests
            current = json.loads(mcontents[0].text)["deployments"][0]
            proposal = await client.call_tool("rollback_deployment", {
                "deployment": service,
                "target_revision": "r183",  # last known-good; in prod: from the report
            })
            pending = proposal.structured_content
            assert pending["status"] == "pending_approval", pending
            trace("remediation_proposed", status=pending["status"],
                  challenge_id=pending["challenge_id"],
                  current_revision=current["revision"], target="r183")
            print(f"\n>>> CHALLENGE {pending['challenge_id']} pending human approval.")
            print(f">>> {pending['instructions']}\n")

            # 5. HITL: wait for the out-of-band token on stdin. In production
            #    this is the on-call engineer pasting the token after review;
            #    the agent blocks here and cannot mint it itself.
            token = await asyncio.to_thread(
                input, "Paste HMAC approval token (empty to abort): ")
            token = token.strip()
            if not token:
                trace("remediation_aborted", challenge_id=pending["challenge_id"])
                return {"status": "aborted"}

            # 6. EXECUTE: the server verifies signature + expiry + single-use.
            result = await client.call_tool("rollback_deployment", {
                "deployment": service,
                "target_revision": "r183",
                "approval_token": token,
            })
            outcome = result.structured_content
            trace("remediation_outcome", **outcome)

            # Drain one rotation event to prove the subscription is live.
            try:
                with _timeout(60):  # longer than any rotation interval in use
                    async for event in sub:
                        trace("resource_updated", uri=event.uri)
                        break
            except TimeoutError:
                trace("resource_updated_timeout")
            return outcome


class _timeout:
    """Tiny sync context manager around anyio.fail_after for readability."""

    def __init__(self, seconds: float) -> None:
        self._seconds = seconds
        self._cm = None

    def __enter__(self):
        import anyio

        self._cm = anyio.fail_after(self._seconds)
        return self._cm.__enter__()

    def __exit__(self, *exc):
        return self._cm.__exit__(*exc)


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Out-of-band approver CLI: `python -m sre_mcp.host approve ...`
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
def approve_cli(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> int:
    """Mint an approval token. Run by the HUMAN, holding the shared secret.

    The agent never sees the secret and never runs this command — that
    separation is the entire security model.
    """
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description="Mint an HMAC approval token (human only).")
    sub = parser.add_subparsers(dest="cmd", required=True)

    ap = sub.add_parser("approve", help="Mint a token for a pending challenge.")
    ap.add_argument("--secret", required=True, help="Shared HMAC secret (from your vault).")
    ap.add_argument("--challenge-id", required=True)
    ap.add_argument("--action", required=True, help="e.g. rollback_deployment")
    ap.add_argument("--target", required=True, help="e.g. payments-api")
    ap.add_argument("--expires-at", required=True, type=float,
                    help="Expiry epoch, copied from the pending challenge.")

    sub.add_parser("triage", help="Run the triage loop.").add_argument(
        "--service", default="payments-api")
    args = parser.parse_args(argv)

    if args.cmd == "approve":
        token = mint_approval_token(
            args.secret, args.challenge_id, args.action, args.target, args.expires_at)
        print(token)
        return 0

    asyncio.run(triage(args.service, "prod-us-east"))
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(approve_cli())

mock_observability/app.py — the compose-only stub:

"""Mock observability HTTP service (docker-compose only).

> Run this on a Docker-equipped machine — not in a sandbox.

Serves the same shapes the in-process MockObservability produces:
log tails, deployment manifests, and metric snapshots. The SRE server talks
to it when SRE_OBSERVABILITY_URL is set.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import sys
import time

sys.path.insert(0, "/app")

from fastapi import FastAPI
from sre_mcp.synthetic import generate_stack_traces, seed_for

app = FastAPI(title="mock-observability")

_DEPLOYMENTS = {
    "prod-us-east": [
        {"name": "payments-api", "cluster": "prod-us-east", "revision": "r184",
         "replicas": 12, "status": "healthy",
         "image": "registry.internal/payments-api:r184"},
        {"name": "orders-api", "cluster": "prod-us-east", "revision": "r211",
         "replicas": 8, "status": "healthy",
         "image": "registry.internal/orders-api:r211"},
    ]
}


@app.get("/logs/{service}")
def get_logs(service: str, lines: int = 200) -> dict:
    all_lines = generate_stack_traces(seed_for(service), 5_000, service)
    return {"service": service, "lines": all_lines[-lines:]}


@app.get("/clusters/{cluster}/deployments")
def get_deployments(cluster: str) -> dict:
    return {"cluster": cluster, "deployments": _DEPLOYMENTS.get(cluster, [])}


@app.get("/clusters/{cluster}/metrics")
def get_metrics(cluster: str) -> dict:
    return {
        "cluster": cluster,
        "captured_at": time.time(),
        "cpu_percent": 78.4,
        "memory_percent": 71.2,
        "p99_latency_ms": 1240.5,
        "error_rate": 0.18,
    }
